giant_bud.name: A bud taller than a person

upward_snow.name: A snowflake falling upwards (in a jar)

ice_cream_plombir.name: Vanilla ice cream in a wafer cup

dragon_egg.name: An egg, warm to the touch

flower_shop_site.name: “Pivonia” flower shop
flower_shop_site.about: A little shop that smells of soil and peonies. They make up bouquets, sell fruit tree saplings, and can arrange a bouquet from your own flowers.

cafe_site.name: “Lypa” café
cafe_site.about: The corner café where people drop in for coffee and the news. Mornings bring a queue with travel mugs, evenings long talks until closing. The cook will gladly take fresh fish.

bakery.name: “Palianytsia” bakery
bakery.about: The bakery opens while it is still dark: by four the palianytsias are going into the oven. Everything is gone by lunch, so don't be late. They'll take your flour too.

grocery.name: “Kolosok” grocery
grocery.about: An ordinary village shop: milk, honey, flour, seeds for the garden. You can bring in vegetables from your own plot here as well.

library_site.name: Library
library_site.about: A quiet library with wooden shelves and lamps over the tables. You can take a book home — just remember to bring it back.

townhall_site.name: Town hall
townhall_site.about: The town hall with a clock over the door. The head of the community sees people here, certificates are issued, and money is collected for the town's shared projects. Closed at weekends.

hardware_site.name: “Maister” hardware store
hardware_site.about: A hardware store that has everything: paint, boards, nails, ladders, fishing rods, buckets. The clerk will tell you what you need for the job.

square_site.name: Square
square_site.about: The heart of Lypove: a fountain, benches and room for fairs and festivals. Someone is always sitting here, even at night.

market_site.name: Market
market_site.about: A market under awnings: vegetables, fruit and odds and ends from the villages around. Busiest in the morning.

school_site.name: School
school_site.about: The village school with its yard and an old maple. On weekdays the bells ring; at weekends it is quiet. The music room has sheet music.

hospital_site.name: Hospital
hospital_site.about: The hospital works day and night: doctors see people by day, a nurse is on duty at night. The pharmacy is here too.

police_site.name: Police station
police_site.about: The police station, where someone is always on duty. People come here when something has happened — by day or by night.

fire_site.name: Fire station
fire_site.about: The fire station with its red gates. They are on duty around the clock — if something is burning, they're already on the way.

post_site.name: Lypove Post Office
post_site.about: The Lypove post office: letters, parcels and a shelf of electronics — phones and laptops are bought here. The postman sets out on the round at seven.

utility_site.name: Utilities office
utility_site.about: The utilities office: pay the electricity and water bills here and ask when the pipe will be fixed. Weekdays only.

workshop_site.name: “Second Life” workshop
workshop_site.about: The “Second Life” workshop mends what others would throw away. The craftsman sells boards and nails and is always glad to look at something you've made.

vet_site.name: “Lapka” vet clinic
vet_site.about: The “Lapka” vet clinic: they treat, vaccinate and feed the stray cats by the door. Pet food is sold here too.

gym_site.name: “Syla” gym
gym_site.about: The “Syla” gym with a punching bag, barbells and a coach who won't let you slack. Open until late in the evening.

bar_site.name: “Zhabka” bar
bar_site.about: The “Zhabka” bar comes alive in the evening: darts, a jukebox, lemonade and local wine. Open past midnight.

playground.name: Playground
playground.about: A playground with swings, a slide and a sandpit. Always open, but noisiest after school.

park_site.name: Lakeside park
park_site.about: The park by the lake: paths, benches and willows over the water. Lovely by day and at sunset.

bread_factory_site.name: “Kolos” bread factory
bread_factory_site.about: The “Kolos” bread factory bakes bread for the whole area. You can mill your own flour here. Most of the work is done before lunch.

water_tower_site.name: Water tower
water_tower_site.about: The old water tower. At the bottom there's a tap with drinking water, at the top a viewing platform overlooking all of Lypove. Climbing is on weekdays only.

church_site.name: St Nicholas Church
church_site.about: A brick church with an old organ. You can light a candle or simply sit in the quiet. Open from morning to evening.

substation_site.name: Substation
substation_site.about: The substation hums quietly behind its fence. From here the light goes to every home in Lypove.

forest_edge.name: Forest edge
forest_edge.about: The edge of the woods at the end of the village: paths, mushrooms after rain and shade in summer. The road to the forest starts here.

hostel_site.name: “Leleka” hostel
hostel_site.about: The “Leleka” hostel for those on the road. You can nap for a few hours at the front desk. The desk is open from morning till late evening.

newsroom_site.name: “The Lypove Herald” newsroom
newsroom_site.about: The newsroom of “The Lypove Herald”. They write about everything that happened that day and take ads for the next issue.

clothes_site.name: “Lon” clothes shop
clothes_site.about: The “Lon” clothes shop: simple things in natural fabrics and scraps for those who sew their own. Closed on Sundays.

salon_site.name: “Lokon” hair salon
salon_site.about: The “Lokon” hair salon: haircuts, styling and the freshest gossip. The hairdresser rests on Sundays and Mondays.

donut_site.name: Ponchykova
donut_site.about: The donut shop: glaze, cherry jam, chocolate and a coffee to go with your donut. Donuts are baked in the morning and sold until evening.

sto_site.name: “Haika” garage
sto_site.about: The “Haika” garage repairs cars from all over the district. There's petrol in cans and a coffee machine for those who wait.

driving_site.name: “Green Light” driving school
driving_site.about: The “Green Light” driving school: theory in the classroom, practice on the streets of Lypove with an instructor. The instructor is in every day except Sunday.

home_old2.name: Grandpa Ostap's cottage on Garden Street

temple_site.name: Temple of the Quiet Lotus
temple_site.about: The Temple of the Quiet Lotus — a place for silence and meditation. A gong, incense, prayer wheels. It opens at dawn.

radio_site.name: “Lypove FM” radio
radio_site.about: “Lypove FM” is on air from morning to evening. You can request a song here and buy a record.

cinema_site.name: “Zoria” cinema
cinema_site.about: The “Zoria” cinema with plush seats and popcorn. Showings from early afternoon until night; a different film at weekends.

cart_stop_1.name: Ice-cream cart stop: Beach by the pier

door:home_old2.name: Grandpa Ostap's cottage on Garden Street

factories.name: Factory end: bread factory, silos, water tower

forest_edge.name: Forest edge (the road to the forest)

square_centre.name: Centre of the square, by the fountain

rock_hill.name: At the foot of the mountain

sawmill.name: Sawmill
sawmill.about: The sawmill in the forest: logs are sawn into boards and beams here. Loud, and it smells of resin. Quiet on Sundays.

forest_glade_site.name: Clearing
forest_glade_site.about: A sunny glade in the forest where the forester keeps things in order. A good place for a rest.

logging.name: Felled woodland
logging.about: The logging site: stumps, stacks of logs and the track they're hauled out along.

grove_site.name: The old circle
grove_site.about: An old circle of stones deep in the woods. No one remembers who put them there.

dump_site.name: Dump
dump_site.about: The dump outside the village. The collector works in the mornings, and at weekends there's a flea market — treasures turn up among the junk.

fields_site.name: Wheat field
fields_site.about: Wheat fields as far as the horizon. Harvest in summer; stubble and birds in autumn.

farm.name: “Linden Grove” farm
farm.about: The “Linden Grove” farm: cows, sheep, hens and a farmer who gets up before the sun.

creamery_site.name: “Ovechka” mini-mill
creamery_site.about: The “Ovechka” mini-mill: wool is spun, scarves are woven and cheese is made here. You can do some of the work yourself.

hippodrome_site.name: “Burevii” racecourse
hippodrome_site.about: The “Burevii” racecourse: stables, a track and stands. The grooms are here from six in the morning, and all of Lypove gathers for the races.

requires.hint: Passes are checked at the gate. The racecourse ticket office is on the notice board by the field.

cave_site.name: Cave
cave_site.about: A cave behind the hill. The old miner knows every turn in it — don't go far without him.

requires.hint: Without a lamp you can't see your own hands in the cave. Grandpa Panas used to work down the mine — maybe he still has a lamp?

winery_site.name: “Loza” winery
winery_site.about: The “Loza” winery among the vineyards. They sell wine from their own vines and keep the barrels in a cool cellar.

requires.hint: The vineyard gates are shut — the vines are drying out. Bohdan the winemaker is looking for a helper by the well at the farm.

cemetery_site.name: Cemetery
cemetery_site.about: A quiet cemetery under the lindens. The caretaker sweeps the paths every day except Sunday.

requires.hint: The tower door is locked. The head of the community has the key — drop by the town hall, he's getting the festival ready.
The hatch is locked with a heavy padlock. They say Iryna the barmaid has the key — and she's looking for something to treat the quiz guests to.
The glass doors are shut. They say on the spring equinox the water draws back and you can see the greenhouse on the other side.
Nothing here but heat. They say on the summer solstice a salt sea shows white beyond the crack.
Somewhere a clock is ticking. They say on the autumn equinox you can see a garden beyond the crack where pages fall from the trees.
“Ponchykova” is still being built: behind the fence it smells of cement, not donuts. Look in once it opens.

marta.name: Marta
marta.about: Runs the “Lypa” café. Remembers how everyone takes their coffee, and always has a spare bun.

0.text: Good morning! The first coffee of the day is the most honest one.

1.text: Buns fresh from the oven. Take one while they're warm.

2.text: The market at this hour is like an orchestra before a concert.

3.text: The fountain whispers the same gossip as my customers.

4.text: Evening is when everyone finally sits down.

5.text: I've made the dough for tomorrow. It's sleeping, and I'll be off soon too.

6.text: You look like you need a mint tea.

7.text: Ostap was reading over a cold coffee again. I brought him another.

8.text: You know, I keep a notebook of who likes what. You're already in it.

9.text: I used to bake only for myself. Now it's for the whole village.

10.text: If you ever can't sleep, come by. I leave the kitchen light on.

11.text: You're like family to me. Just don't tell Panas — he's jealous of my pies.

12.text: What a cosy place you have! I'd bake here every Sunday.

13.text: Your place smells like home. That's the highest praise a baker can give.

14.text: The sun is gentle today. Like butter on warm bread.

15.text: The beach is so quiet in the evening. I bring a flask down there.

chatter.0: The dough rose like never before today!
chatter.1: Have you tried my cherry pies yet?
chatter.2: They say something was glowing over the lake last night.
chatter.3: Come in for a coffee while it's hot.
chatter.4: I could use another pair of hands in the kitchen…

greet.1: Oh, it's you! Come in for a coffee.

0.text: I need three apples for a pie. Would you bring some from the orchard?
0.thanks: Oh, how rosy they are! This pie will be enough for the whole square.

1.text: I want to make jam. Two handfuls of any berries?
1.thanks: The jam will be finger-licking good. Here's a teapot, so you've got something to drink it with.

2.text: The fish soup is short of fish. Any kind will do!
2.thanks: The fish soup will be fit for a king today!

0.text: I baked too many buns, and one is definitely yours. You'll find it in the basket by the door. Marta

1.text: You're like family in this village now. Here's my old teapot — it has seen a lot of good conversations. Marta

ostap.name: Ostap
ostap.about: The librarian. Speaks softly, knows by heart where every book stands, and collects other people's stories.

0.text: Shh… oh, we're outside. Hello.

1.text: Someone returned a book today with a pressed daisy inside.

2.text: The water in the pond looks like a page nobody has written yet.

3.text: Lunchtime coffee at Marta's is the only punctuation in my day.

4.text: The morning smells of paper and dew.

5.text: In the evenings I count the frogs. There's always one more than yesterday.

6.text: Do you like quiet too? It's of very good quality here.

7.text: I keep a catalogue of the village's stories. You'll go in the “New Neighbours” chapter.

8.text: Myron says the stars are a library you can only read at night.

9.text: I rarely say this, but it's easy to be quiet with you.

10.text: One day I want to write a book about this place. You'll be on the first page.

11.text: You have so much light here. Books would be happy in it.

12.text: May I sit for a while? It's easier to think here than in the reading room.

13.text: Rain or shine — the books wait all the same.

14.text: This oak remembers more than all my books.

15.text: Under the oak, reading feels different. Slower.

chatter.0: Have you read about the old oak in the forest?
chatter.2: A new little shelf has appeared in the library.
chatter.3: I wonder who built this bridge first.
chatter.4: The clouds today are like punctuation marks.

0.text: I need a feather — to write the way people used to.
0.thanks: A lovely quill. I'll write the first line about you.

1.text: My herbarium is missing an acorn.
1.thanks: An acorn is a little oak that doesn't yet know what it will become.

2.text: A pretty seashell for the shelf of books about the sea?
2.thanks: Now there'll be a sea in the library too. Here — this is for you.

0.text: I found a book that reminded me of you. Here you go. O.

solomiia.name: Solomiia
solomiia.about: A painter. Paints light on water, and people when they aren't looking. Always has paint on her fingers.

0.text: Wait! No, nothing. The light on you is just lovely.

1.text: Morning light is like a watercolour that hasn't dried yet.

2.text: The pond is pink today. I can't paint it fast enough.

3.text: The people on the square are the best models. They don't know they're posing.

4.text: The evening shadows are so long you could hide in them.

5.text: At night the paints sleep, but I don't.

6.text: Have I got paint on my nose? Again?

7.text: I painted Marta with a bun. She said I gave her three chins. Not true — two.

8.text: Would you like me to paint your house one day? With a cat on the windowsill.

9.text: I rarely show unfinished work. I'll show it to you.

10.text: You're my favourite colour in this village. I just don't know its name yet.

11.text: What a composition! May I sit and paint for a while?

12.text: Everything in your home is in its place. Like in a good painting.

13.text: The hill by day is one big green sky.

14.text: A campfire is the best model. It never sits still.

15.text: On the beach I paint the waves. They're different every time.

16.text: This oak is a whole painting without a frame.

chatter.1: Did you see the light on the water?
chatter.2: I need blue paint. Lots of blue.
chatter.3: You look like an evening landscape.
chatter.4: One day I'll paint you by the fountain.

0.text: Three wildflowers for my still life, please.
0.thanks: Oh, those colours! I'll paint them today.

1.text: Could you bring me a poppy? I want to mix a red from it.
1.thanks: I'll name this red after you.

2.text: Amber is sunshine in stone. Could you find some on the beach?
2.thanks: It glows! Here, take a painting — with that very light.

0.text: Here's a sketch of your house. Hang it up if you like it! Solomiia

panas.name: Grandpa Panas
panas.about: Gardener and fisherman. Knows every garden bed by name and believes tomatoes love songs.

0.text: Ah, neighbour! Did you see how the carrots shot up? Proud as anything in the sun.

1.text: Fish are honest in the morning — they bite or they don't.

2.text: Tomatoes need singing to. Don't laugh, they can hear.

3.text: Everything at the market gets dearer, except a kind word.

4.text: I'm too old to hurry. The earth doesn't hurry either.

5.text: Evening is the time to sit on the bench and grumble about the weather.

6.text: Yarynka ran off somewhere again. That child is like the wind.

7.text: Once there was nothing here but a meadow and me with a spade.

8.text: Here's a secret: cucumbers like it when you praise them out loud.

9.text: My granny used to say: where there's a garden, there's a home. You've got both now.

10.text: You're like a grandchild to me. Whichever suits you. What matters is you're family.

11.text: My, how well you keep everything! Not a single weed.

12.text: Let me have a look at your garden beds… Good! Very good.

13.text: I'm not asleep. I'm listening to the grass grow.

14.text: The forest lake is my secret place. Now it's yours too.

15.text: The apple trees are better than ever this year.

chatter.0: The tomatoes are in a good mood today.
chatter.1: In my day the river was wider.
chatter.3: It'll rain. My knee says so.

0.text: Three pine cones for kindling. Old bones get cold.

0.text: Here's a barrel — rainwater is the best thing for a garden. Panas

yarynka.name: Yarynka
yarynka.about: Panas's granddaughter, delivers the post by bike. Knows all the news before it even happens.

0.text: Hi-hi! No letter for you. But there could have been!

1.text: Heard the news? No? Me neither, yet, but there'll be some soon!

2.text: I rode round the square three times and didn't fall once. A record!

3.text: There's a frog in the pond called the General. I named her.

4.text: Morning! The best time for post and buns.

5.text: In the evening I have to tell Grandpa everything that happened. Everything.

6.text: Ostap says I talk faster than I think. But I think fast!

7.text: Want me to bring you the news first? For free!

8.text: I haven't told anyone yet, but I want to be a traveller.

9.text: You don't laugh at my ideas. That's rare.

10.text: When I go travelling, you'll be the first one I write to!

11.text: Wow, your house is like a fairy tale! Can I look at everything?

12.text: Can I rest here a bit? My legs keep pedalling on their own.

13.text: You can see the whole village from the hill! Even your roof!

14.text: Berries! Want some? Oops, I ate them all.

15.text: Shall we swim to the little boat?

chatter.2: I saw a fox in the forest!
chatter.3: Grandpa's talking to the tomatoes again.
chatter.4: Can I have a go in the boat?

0.text: Raspberries! Two handfuls! Pretty please!
0.thanks: Mmm! I'll give half to Grandpa. Maybe.

1.text: I need two flat pebbles — for skimming stones!

2.text: A shell for my sea-treasure collection?

0.text: I found something strange in Grandpa's attic. I'll tell you when I see you!!! Y.

lines.1: It's a map! A really old one. Here's the forest, the lake… and here — a cross by the big oak.
lines.2: Grandpa says it's "the follies of youth". But his ears went red!
lines.3: Will you help me figure it out? Not a word to anyone!

lines.2: But I need an acorn from that oak — for luck. Will you bring one?

lines.0: Grandpa's little boat lies by the lake. Old, but sturdy!

lines.2: Three pine cones and she'll float again!

taras.name: Taras
taras.about: Musician. Plays on the square in the evenings and believes every day has its own tune.

olena.name: Olena
olena.about: Flower seller from the market. Makes bouquets to suit your mood and knows how to be quiet with you.

myron.name: Myron
myron.about: Amateur astronomer. Spends his nights on the hill with a telescope; sleepy and dreamy by day.

0.text: Oh… good… what time is it? Daytime? Sorry, I'm still on night time.

1.text: Cassiopeia will be visible tonight. Come up to the hill.

2.text: Look: over there is the Plough. And there's my favourite empty patch of sky.

3.text: Stars are like the windows of other people's houses. Someone lives in every one.

4.text: Marta's coffee keeps me awake until sunset.

5.text: Ostap lends me books about the stars. I give them back with notes in the margins.

6.text: Evening is the overture to the night.

7.text: I once made a wish on a shooting star. It came true: I'm here.

8.text: Have you ever wondered whether someone is looking at us from those stars?

9.text: I named a little star after you. Unofficially.

10.text: You shine steadily. Like the North Star. Someone to rely on.

11.text: You must get a lovely view of the sky from your window.

12.text: It's quiet here, like on the hill. Mind if I nap a bit? Kidding. Or not.

13.text: In the morning the stars hide, and so do I.

14.text: Sparks from the campfire fly up to the stars. Maybe they were sparks once too.

15.text: The water reflects the stars. Two skies instead of one.

chatter.0: There'll be a meteor shower tonight.
chatter.1: I didn't get enough sleep. As usual.
chatter.2: Did you see Venus over the hill?
chatter.3: Stars are letters from the past.
chatter.4: By the campfire you can see sparks — like tiny comets.

0.text: Two pine cones. For the telescope. Don't ask.
0.thanks: Now it stands level. The stars will thank you.

1.text: Something shiny from the beach? Amber would be a marvel.
1.thanks: It's like a frozen star. Here, take a jar of fireflies.

2.text: A night fish — an eel. They say eels swim after the stars.
2.thanks: Now I know: the stars and the fish look at each other.

0.text: Here's a star lantern. So you always have a little piece of sky at home. M.

st.fountain.wish.label: Toss a coin
st.fountain.wish.text: The coin clinks against the bottom. Your wish is made — just don't tell anyone.
st.fountain.wish.spent: Enough wishes for today — give these a chance to come true.

st.fountain.charm.label: Search the bottom for a charm
st.fountain.charm.text: Among the coins glints a bit of glass on a string. Someone made a wish and forgot it — now it's yours.
st.fountain.charm.spent: Only coins on the bottom. Charms don't turn up every day.

st.notice_board.read.label: Read the notices
st.notice_board.read.text: “Lost: ginger cat, answers to ‘Pyrizhok’.” “Bike for sale, hardly bites.” “Saturday — community clean-up by the school.”
st.notice_board.read.spent: You've already read every scrap on the board.

st.telescope.stars.label: Look at the stars
st.telescope.stars.text: You find the Milky Way and the Plough — and copy them onto a scrap of paper.
st.telescope.stars.spent: The sky has clouded over — the stars are hiding.

st.stall_bread.bun.label: Buy a bun
st.stall_bread.bun.text: Still warm, with poppy seeds. The baker winks: “The second one — tomorrow!”
st.stall_bread.bun.spent: The buns are gone; only crumbs are left on the stall.

st.stall_veg.carrot.label: Buy carrots
st.stall_veg.carrot.text: Sweet, straight from the garden, with soil still on their tails.

st.stall_veg.potato.label: Buy potatoes
st.stall_veg.potato.text: Three potatoes — just right for potato pancakes.
st.stall_veg.potato.spent: The potatoes are gone — the seller is folding up her sacks.

st.stall_veg.seeds.label: Buy sunflower seeds
st.stall_veg.seeds.text: A handful of roasted seeds — some for the birds, some for you.

st.stall_flowers.bouquet.label: Buy a bouquet
st.stall_flowers.bouquet.text: The florist wraps the bouquet in kraft paper and ties it with a ribbon.
st.stall_flowers.bouquet.spent: The bouquets were snapped up this morning.

st.market.buyer.label: Second-hand buyer: sell from the inventory
st.market.buyer.text: The buyer turns the thing over in their hands, names a price and counts the coins out of a tin.
st.market.buyer.spent: The buyer waves a hand: "That's enough for today, the tin is empty. Come back tomorrow."

st.carousel.ride.label: Ride the carousel
st.carousel.ride.text: The little horses run in a circle, the world blurs, and you laugh like a child.
st.carousel.ride.spent: The carousel keeper is oiling the works — that's it for today.

st.swing.swing.label: Have a swing
st.swing.swing.text: Higher, higher still — you can see the rooftops and the top of the church.
st.swing.swing.spent: The kids are on the swings now — it's their turn.

st.birdbath.feed.label: Scatter seeds for the birds
st.birdbath.feed.text: Sparrows flock in from everywhere. A little tit leaves you a feather to remember it by.
st.birdbath.feed.spent: The birds have eaten their fill and are dozing on the branches.

st.bakery.bread.label: Buy a palianytsia
st.bakery.bread.text: A warm palianytsia, still smelling of the oven.
st.bakery.bread.spent: The bakery has sold all its palianytsias.

st.bakery.pie.label: Buy an apple pie
st.bakery.pie.text: A slice? No — the whole pie. The baker doesn't even ask.
st.bakery.pie.spent: The last pie was just taken.

st.bakery.flour.label: Sell flour to the baker
st.bakery.flour.text: “Now that's flour! Fine as down,” — the baker counts out the coins.
st.bakery.flour.spent: The baker already has plenty of flour.

st.bakery.bake_pie.label: Bake a pie in the oven
st.bakery.bake_pie.text: Apples, flour, an egg — and half an hour later the whole bakery smells of cinnamon.
st.bakery.bake_pie.spent: The oven is cooling down — the baker closes the door.

st.cafe.coffee.label: Get a coffee to go
st.cafe.coffee.text: The barista draws a linden leaf in the foam.
st.cafe.coffee.spent: The coffee machine has overheated — the waitress waves: “That's enough coffee for today!”

st.cafe.cocoa.label: Get a cocoa
st.cafe.cocoa.text: Cocoa with foam and a marshmallow on top. Warms your hands and your heart.

st.cafe.lemonade.label: Get a lemonade
st.cafe.lemonade.text: Cold, with mint. Ice clinks against the glass.
st.cafe.lemonade.spent: The lemonade has been drunk to the last drop.

st.cafe.fish.label: Give the fish to the cook
st.cafe.fish.text: “That'll go in the fish soup!” — the cook takes your catch and pours coins into your palm.
st.cafe.fish.spent: The cook says there's enough fish for today — the fridge is full.

st.grocery.fruit.label: Sell fruit
st.grocery.fruit.text: The shopkeeper weighs the apples on old scales and nods, pleased.
st.grocery.fruit.spent: The shop has bought enough fruit already; they won't take more.

st.grocery.berries.label: Sell berries
st.grocery.berries.text: “Wild ones? Real ones?” — and she's already setting them out in little baskets.
st.grocery.berries.spent: There are enough berries already — the shopkeeper spreads her hands.

st.grocery.mushrooms.label: Sell mushrooms
st.grocery.mushrooms.text: Mushrooms sell out at the shop before lunch.
st.grocery.mushrooms.spent: Someone already brought a full basket of mushrooms today.

st.grocery.milk.label: Buy milk
st.grocery.milk.text: A bottle of farm milk, with cream on top.

st.grocery.honey.label: Buy honey
st.grocery.honey.text: Linden honey from the apiary behind the farm. It stretches like sunbeams.
st.grocery.honey.spent: The honey's run out; a new batch is coming from the apiary.

st.flowers.make_bouquet.label: Make a bouquet from your own flowers
st.flowers.make_bouquet.text: The florist shows you how to set a poppy among the daisies. It looks lovely!
st.flowers.make_bouquet.spent: Petro has already made all the bouquets he had for today.

st.flowers.buy.label: Buy a bouquet
st.flowers.buy.text: Peonies, lisianthus and a sprig of eucalyptus.
st.flowers.buy.spent: No bouquets left — only greenery in the window.

st.library.borrow.label: Borrow a book
st.library.borrow.text: The librarian stamps it and whispers: “Just don't fold the pages.”
st.library.borrow.spent: The librarian gently reminds you: first read the one you have at home.

st.library.return.label: Return a book
st.library.return.text: The book goes back on the shelf, and a whole story stays in your head.

st.church.candle.label: Light a candle
st.church.candle.text: A small flame flickers among the others. Your heart grows quiet.

st.church.organ.label: Listen to the organ
st.church.organ.text: The organist is rehearsing. The sound fills the church right up to the vault.

st.cemetery.flowers.label: Lay flowers
st.cemetery.flowers.text: You lay a bouquet on the old stone. Someone once came here just like this.

st.radio.song.label: Request a song
st.radio.song.text: The host reads your greeting on air. Your song plays all down the street!
st.radio.song.spent: The airtime is booked until evening.

st.radio.record.label: Buy a radio record
st.radio.record.text: A record of “Lypove FM”'s greatest hits, signed by the host.

st.newsroom.ad.label: Place an ad in the paper
st.newsroom.ad.text: The editor promises to put it next to the weather forecast. The best spot!
st.newsroom.ad.spent: The ad is already in this issue — there's no room for more.

st.newsroom.paper.label: Leaf through the latest issue
st.newsroom.paper.text: It smells of printer's ink. On the front page — news you may have made yourself.
st.newsroom.paper.spent: You've read the latest issue from the first page to the last.

st.townhall.postcard.label: Take a postcard of the town
st.townhall.postcard.text: The secretary pulls out a postcard with the town hall and the lindens: “A keepsake!”

st.gym.train.label: Work out
st.gym.train.text: Half an hour on the treadmill — and your legs say “thank you” (a little later).
st.gym.train.spent: The trainer says: “That's enough for today, your muscles need a rest.”

st.gym.box.label: Pound the punching bag
st.gym.box.text: The trainer shows you a proper jab. Again! Again!
st.gym.box.spent: The bag is still swinging — your arms are buzzing.

st.vet.stray.label: Feed the stray cat
st.vet.stray.text: The ginger cat eats the fish, purrs and falls asleep right on your hand.
st.vet.stray.spent: The kitty is full and asleep.

st.hostel.rest.label: Nap after the journey
st.hostel.rest.text: The bed creaks, the town hums outside the window. You wake up rested.

st.bar.lemonade.label: Order a lemonade
st.bar.lemonade.text: The barmaid drops two cherries into the glass: “One's on the house.”
st.bar.lemonade.spent: The barmaid spreads her hands: the lemonade's run out.

st.bar.wine.label: Sell wine to the bar
st.bar.wine.text: “A real ‘Loza’? I'll take it!” — the bottle goes up on the top shelf.
st.bar.wine.spent: The bar has plenty of wine already.

st.bar.jukebox.label: Play a song on the jukebox
st.bar.jukebox.text: The coin is swallowed, the record drops — and the whole bar sings along.
st.bar.jukebox.spent: The jukebox swallowed the coin and went quiet.

st.bar.darts.label: Throw darts
st.bar.darts.text: Seven, twenty, and… bullseye! Someone at a table applauds.
st.bar.darts.spent: Someone has already taken the darts.

st.tower.lookout.label: Climb up to the lookout
st.tower.lookout.text: From here you can see all of Lypove: the roofs, the field, the windmills and the dark strip of forest.
st.tower.lookout.spent: The keeper is closing the lookout.

st.tower.water.label: Get water from the tap
st.tower.water.text: The water from the tower is cold and smells a little of iron.
st.tower.water.spent: The tap hisses — the water's off until morning.

st.forest.campfire.label: Warm up by the campfire
st.forest.campfire.text: Brushwood crackles, sparks fly up to the stars. It smells of smoke and baked potatoes.

st.forest.bake_potato.label: Bake potatoes in the embers
st.forest.bake_potato.text: You burn your fingers, blow on them — and eat them, ash and all. The tastiest thing in the world.

st.forest.lookout.label: Climb the fire tower
st.forest.lookout.text: Forest all the way to the horizon, and not a wisp of smoke anywhere. The forester waves to you from below.
st.forest.lookout.spent: The forester has locked the tower.

st.forest.sawmill.label: Help at the sawmill
st.forest.sawmill.text: You pass the planks, the saw sings. The sawyers share their lunch and their pay with you.
st.forest.sawmill.spent: The sawmill has stopped — the workers are having tea.

st.farm.milk.label: Milk the cow
st.farm.milk.text: Zirka stands still and swishes her tail at your ear only once.
st.farm.milk.spent: The cow was already milked this morning.

st.farm.eggs.label: Collect the eggs
st.farm.eggs.text: The hens cluck indignantly but give them up. One egg is still warm.
st.farm.eggs.spent: The hens have already laid — the nests are empty.

st.farm.well.label: Draw water from the well
st.farm.well.text: The bucket rattles down on its chain, and icy water rises from the depths.
st.farm.well.spent: The bucket is at the bottom already — let the water gather.

st.farm.honey.label: Collect honey
st.farm.honey.text: In a veil and gloves, slowly, slowly… The bees aren't pleased, but the honey is yours.
st.farm.honey.spent: The bees are cross — let them rest.

st.farm.shear.label: Shear a sheep
st.farm.shear.text: Bebeshka the sheep puts up with it, because she knows: summer is easier without a fur coat.
st.farm.shear.spent: The sheep have already been sheared.

st.farm.corn.label: Pick corn
st.farm.corn.text: The cobs rustle, and yellow kernels peek out of each one.
st.farm.corn.spent: The corn has already been picked.

st.farm.hay.label: Gather hay
st.farm.hay.text: The hay prickles and smells of summer, even in winter.
st.farm.hay.spent: The hay has already been raked up.

st.farm.feed.label: Feed the livestock
st.farm.feed.text: The cows reach for the hay, and the farmer thanks you with a coin: “What a helper!”
st.farm.feed.spent: The livestock has already been fed.

st.creamery.cheese.label: Make cheese
st.creamery.cheese.text: The milk thickens, and the cheesemaker shows you how to cut the curd. In a week — cheese!
st.creamery.cheese.spent: The cheese dairy is full — the cheeses are ripening.

st.creamery.spin.label: Spin yarn
st.creamery.spin.text: The wheel hums, the wool draws out into an even thread. It takes a while, but it works.
st.creamery.spin.spent: The spinning wheel stands still: Uliana says they've spun enough for today.

st.creamery.scarf.label: Weave a scarf
st.creamery.scarf.text: The shuttle flies back and forth. The scarf comes out warm and a bit crooked — just as it should.

st.creamery.mittens.label: Knit mittens
st.creamery.mittens.text: Stitch by stitch — and here's a pair of mittens with a fir-tree pattern.

st.creamery.pouch.label: Sew a little bag
st.creamery.pouch.text: The cheesemaker sews you a drawstring bag from your wool: “Now you can carry more!”
st.creamery.pouch.spent: The seamstress is already sewing another bag.

st.creamery.sell_cheese.label: Hand in cheese for sale
st.creamery.sell_cheese.text: Your cheese goes in the shop window with a sign: “From our neighbour”.
st.creamery.sell_cheese.spent: There's enough cheese on the shelves already.

st.fields.wheat.label: Reap wheat
st.fields.wheat.text: The sickle rustles, the ears fall into a sheaf. A stork circles over the field.
st.fields.wheat.spent: This patch has already been reaped — let the ears grow back.

st.fields.pass.label: Buy a racecourse pass
st.fields.pass.text: On the board — the “Burevii” racecourse ticket office: “Season pass. The horses are waiting!”
st.fields.pass.spent: The racecourse ticket office has closed.

st.factory.mill.label: Grind flour
st.factory.mill.text: The millstones rumble, and white, warm flour pours from the chute.
st.factory.mill.spent: The mill has stopped — the miller is sweeping up the flour.

st.vineyard.grapes.label: Pick grapes
st.vineyard.grapes.text: The bunches are heavy and warm from the sun. One grape for you, the rest into the basket.
st.vineyard.grapes.spent: These vines have already been picked.

st.vineyard.juice.label: Press the juice
st.vineyard.juice.text: Feet in the vat — and laughter all over the vineyard. The juice is ever so sweet.
st.vineyard.juice.spent: The press has already been washed.

st.winery.wine.label: Put the wine in a barrel
st.winery.wine.text: The winemaker pours your grape juice into an oak barrel and chalks your name on it.

st.winery.buy.label: Buy a bottle of wine
st.winery.buy.text: “Last autumn's harvest. It was a good year,” says the winemaker.
st.winery.buy.spent: The bottles are sold out for today.

st.hippodrome.race.label: Watch a race
st.hippodrome.race.text: The horses fly round the track, the stands roar. Burevii wins by half a head!

st.hippodrome.horse.label: Treat a horse to a carrot
st.hippodrome.horse.text: The horse crunches the carrot and nudges you with its nose. The groom gives you an old horseshoe: “For luck.”
st.hippodrome.horse.spent: Burevii has had his fill of carrots.

st.cave.minecart.label: Ride the mine cart
st.cave.minecart.text: The rails creak, the lantern sways, and crystals flash in the dark.
st.cave.minecart.spent: The cart is stuck — they'll grease it tomorrow.

st.stall_bread.sesame_balls.label: Buy sesame balls
st.stall_bread.sesame_balls.text: Crunchy outside, chewy inside. “For a sweet year!” says the baker.

requires.hint: These treats are only baked for Lunar New Year.

st.stall_bread.nian_gao.label: Buy nian gao
st.stall_bread.nian_gao.text: A sticky rice cake: the higher it rises, the higher the year will rise.

requires.hint: These treats are only baked for Lunar New Year.

st.stall_bread.moon_cake.label: Buy a mooncake
st.stall_bread.moon_cake.text: With a dragon pattern on the crust.

requires.hint: These treats are only baked for Lunar New Year.

st.fair.kutia_wheat.label: Wheat for kutia
st.fair.kutia_wheat.text: A man at the fair scoops out two handfuls of wheat: “For kutia — no haggling.”

st.fair.poppy.label: Poppy seeds for kutia
st.fair.poppy.text: Blue-grey poppy seeds, already rinsed. “Don't forget to grind them,” says the seller.

st.fair.dried.label: Dried fruit for uzvar
st.fair.dried.text: Apples, pears and plums, dried back in summer.

st.fair.pancakes.label: Pancakes from the stall
st.fair.pancakes.text: Maslenytsia! Pancakes with sour cream straight from the pan.

st.fair.pysanka.label: A pysanka from the craftswoman
st.fair.pysanka.text: Red, with an eight-pointed star — the craftswoman spent a whole week painting them.

st.fair.gingerbread.label: Honey gingerbread
st.fair.gingerbread.text: An iced gingerbread on a string: on Honey Feast Day it's a must.

st.fair.apples.label: Apples for the Saviour's Feast
st.fair.apples.text: A basket of apples to take for blessing.

st.fair.flags.label: Little flag
st.fair.flags.text: Blue and yellow, on a stick. On Independence Day the whole square is full of them.

st.fair.nicholas.label: A Saint Nicholas cookie
st.fair.nicholas.text: A little gingerbread shaped like Saint Nicholas — for the good children and the not-so-good.

st.grocery.flour.label: Buy flour
st.grocery.flour.text: A bag of top-grade flour from the “Kolos” bakery.

st.grocery.seed_tomato.label: Tomato seeds
st.grocery.seed_tomato.text: A packet with a picture on the wrapper. The seller advises sowing while it's warm.

st.grocery.seed_cucumber.label: Cucumber seeds
st.grocery.seed_cucumber.text: A packet with a picture on the wrapper. The seller advises sowing while it's warm.

st.grocery.seed_carrot.label: Carrot seeds
st.grocery.seed_carrot.text: A packet with a picture on the wrapper. The seller advises sowing while it's warm.

st.grocery.seed_potato.label: Seed potatoes for planting
st.grocery.seed_potato.text: A packet with a picture on the wrapper. The seller advises sowing while it's warm.

st.grocery.seed_cabbage.label: Cabbage seeds
st.grocery.seed_cabbage.text: A packet with a picture on the wrapper. The seller advises sowing while it's warm.

st.grocery.seed_pumpkin.label: Pumpkin seeds
st.grocery.seed_pumpkin.text: A packet with a picture on the wrapper. The seller advises sowing while it's warm.

st.grocery.seed_strawberry.label: Strawberry seedlings
st.grocery.seed_strawberry.text: A packet with a picture on the wrapper. The seller advises sowing while it's warm.

st.grocery.seed_dill.label: Dill seeds
st.grocery.seed_dill.text: A packet with a picture on the wrapper. The seller advises sowing while it's warm.

st.grocery.seed_sunflower.label: Sunflower seeds
st.grocery.seed_sunflower.text: A packet with a picture on the wrapper. The seller advises sowing while it's warm.

st.flowers.sapling_apple.label: Apple sapling
st.flowers.sapling_apple.text: Mr Petro wraps the roots in damp sacking: “Plant them — and in a year you'll have fruit.”

st.flowers.sapling_cherry.label: Cherry sapling
st.flowers.sapling_cherry.text: Mr Petro wraps the roots in damp sacking: “Plant them — and in a year you'll have fruit.”

st.flowers.sapling_pear.label: Pear sapling
st.flowers.sapling_pear.text: Mr Petro wraps the roots in damp sacking: “Plant them — and in a year you'll have fruit.”

st.flowers.sapling_plum.label: Plum sapling
st.flowers.sapling_plum.text: Mr Petro wraps the roots in damp sacking: “Plant them — and in a year you'll have fruit.”

st.grocery.sell_veg.label: Sell vegetables from the garden
st.grocery.sell_veg.text: The seller weighs them, praises them and counts out the coins: “Home-grown always tastes better than shipped-in.”

st.icecream.buy.label: Buy an ice cream
st.icecream.buy.text: The seller scoops a ball of plombir and pours cherry syrup over it.
st.icecream.buy.spent: The ice cream's finished for today — the seller is already washing the spoons.

st.coffee_cart.coffee.label: Coffee to go
st.coffee_cart.coffee.text: Hot, with cinnamon. Steam rises from the cup.
st.coffee_cart.coffee.spent: The coffee man has packed up his cart and gone off to warm up.

st.flower_cart.bouquet.label: Buy a little bouquet
st.flower_cart.bouquet.text: Tulips wrapped in a copy of “The Lypove Herald”.
st.flower_cart.bouquet.spent: The flowers are all gone for today.

st.book_stall.book.label: Buy a book
st.book_stall.book.text: An old book with someone's inscription on the flyleaf — the best kind.
st.book_stall.book.spent: The interesting books are all gone for today.

st.bandstand.concert.label: Listen to the band
st.bandstand.concert.text: Trumpets, a drum and an old waltz. Couples twirl by the bandstand.
st.bandstand.concert.spent: The band has already packed up their instruments.

st.forest.planks.label: Buy planks
st.forest.planks.text: The sawyers measure the planks and tie them with twine.
st.forest.planks.spent: No more planks today — the sawmill is resting.

st.workshop.nails.label: Buy nails
st.workshop.nails.text: The craftsman pours a handful of nails into a paper bag.

st.workshop.kit.label: Buy a repair kit
st.workshop.kit.text: Glue, screws, sandpaper, a couple of patches — all in a tin box.

st.workshop.sell.label: Show your work to the craftsman
st.workshop.sell.text: The craftsman turns your piece over in his hands, hums — and pays as for a good thing.

st.clothes.cloth.label: Take some fabric scraps
st.clothes.cloth.text: The seller lets the offcuts go for pennies: “Happy sewing.”

st.forest.clay.label: Dig some clay
st.forest.clay.text: By the reeds the clay is rich and blue-grey — just right for a little pot.

requires.hint: You can't dig clay with bare hands — you need a spade.

st.forest.firewood.label: Chop firewood
st.forest.firewood.text: The axe rings, logs fly in every direction. It smells of resin.

requires.hint: Firewood is chopped with an axe.

st.village.leaves.label: Rake leaves in the park
st.village.leaves.text: Swish-swish with the rake — and a yellow pile up to the sky. The caretaker thanks you and pays on behalf of the town.

requires.hint: Leaves are raked with a rake.

st.dump.scrap.label: Look for scrap iron
st.dump.scrap.text: Among the junk — a spring, a bracket and a piece of tin. They'll come in handy.

st.dump.flea.label: Flea market: sell your work
st.dump.flea.text: At weekends people spread out blankets full of all sorts of things. Your piece is the first to go.

st.library.craft_book.label: Take “Make It at Home”
st.library.craft_book.text: An old book of plans: a shelf, a frame, a clay pot. Someone has pencilled tips in the margins.

st.post.phone.label: Buy a smartphone
st.post.phone.text: Brand new, in its box. The postwoman switches it on and shows you where the camera is.
st.post.phone.spent: The smartphones are gone for today — more are coming tomorrow.

st.post.laptop.label: Buy a laptop
st.post.laptop.text: Thin, light, with a “Lypove” sticker on the lid.
st.post.laptop.spent: The laptops have run out for today.

st.hardware.hammer.label: Buy: a hammer

st.temple.buy_incense.label: Take some incense
st.temple.buy_incense.text: The keeper wraps a little bundle of sticks in thin paper: “Sandalwood. It smells like the quiet after rain.”
st.temple.buy_incense.spent: All the incense is given out for today — more comes tomorrow.

st.temple.incense.label: Light the incense
st.temple.incense.text: The smoke rises in a thin thread, and your thoughts slowly settle, like leaves on water.
st.temple.incense.spent: The incense is still smouldering — let it burn down.

st.temple.offer_fruit.label: Leave an offering
st.temple.offer_fruit.text: You lay the fruit among the other gifts. The keeper softly rings a little bell: “Let the heavy drift away and the good come back.” Your heart feels lighter, as if an old stain had been washed away.
st.temple.offer_fruit.spent: You've already brought a gift today. The keeper smiles: “One is enough.”

st.temple.offer_flowers.label: Lay flowers
st.temple.offer_flowers.text: The flowers settle beside the little lamp. In a week they'll wilt — and that too has its lesson, says the keeper.
st.temple.offer_flowers.spent: Flowers are already here — bring fresh ones tomorrow.

st.temple.gong.label: Strike the gong
st.temple.gong.text: Bo-o-ong… The sound circles the hall and takes a long time to fade.
st.temple.gong.spent: The gong is still humming — let it rest.

st.temple.wheels.label: Turn the prayer wheels
st.temple.wheels.text: The wheels creak and roll round. They say every turn is a good wish for someone far away.

st.grove.bow.label: Bow to the idol
st.grove.bow.text: The old oak looks out with four faces to the four winds. The wind rustles in the pines, and it seems someone nodded back.
st.grove.bow.spent: The idol has already seen you today.

st.grove.ribbon.label: Tie a ribbon for a wish
st.grove.ribbon.text: Your ribbon joins a hundred others — faded, fresh, every colour. Each one is somebody's hope.
st.grove.ribbon.spent: One ribbon a day — that's the custom here.

st.grove.circle.label: Join the circle
st.grove.circle.text: Full moon. The fire crackles, torches throw shadows across the stones. People join hands and sing without words — and so do you. When the song dies away, the moon stands right above the idol.
st.grove.circle.spent: The circle has already welcomed you tonight.

st.hardware.ribbon.label: Buy a ribbon
st.hardware.ribbon.text: The seller measures out a metre of ribbon: “For a present or for a wish?”

st.cinema.ticket.label: Buy a ticket
st.cinema.ticket.text: The cashier tears off a ticket: “The show starts soon, sit wherever you like.”
st.cinema.ticket.spent: “We're sold out tonight — the hall is full.”

st.cinema.popcorn.label: Buy popcorn
st.cinema.popcorn.text: Warm, salty, in a paper cup — half of it spills before you reach the hall.

st.cinema.film.label: Watch the film
st.cinema.film.text: The lights go down and the projector starts to whirr. Tonight it's “The Brave Hearts of Lypove”, about the firefighters who saved the bridge. The audience laughs, cries and applauds.
st.cinema.film.spent: The show's already been — a new one tomorrow.

st.cinema.film_weekend.label: Watch the film
st.cinema.film_weekend.text: The weekend show: the good old fairy tale “The Star Fox”. The kids in the front row whisper the lines along with the heroes.
st.cinema.film_weekend.spent: The show's already been — a new one tomorrow.

st.vet.pet_food.label: Buy pet food
st.vet.pet_food.text: The vet scoops food into a paper bag: “This will last a good while.”

help.old_miner.title: Old miner's lamp
help.old_miner.text: Once I spent twenty years going down the mine under Rocky Hill. My old lamp still shines — but the wick is worn and the glass is cracked. Bring me three pine cones for kindling and a skein of yarn for a new wick — I'll mend it and give it to you. Without light, don't take a step in the cave.
help.old_miner.thanks: There, it shines like new! Look after it. And they say the crystals deep in the cave sing…

help.vineyard.title: The Thirsty Vineyard
help.vineyard.text: It's been a dry summer, the vines are wilting and our pump is broken. Bring three jugs of spring water from the well at the farm and an armful of hay to mulch the roots. Then I'll open the vineyard to you: pick as much as you can carry!
help.vineyard.thanks: The vines are alive again! The vineyard gate is always open to you.

help.cellar_key.title: Snacks for Quiz Night
help.cellar_key.text: Quiz night is on Friday, and we've got zero snacks. Two palianytsia loaves and a wheel of cheese will save the evening! And I… I'll give you the key to the cellar. Nobody's been down there for ages — they say there's a passage behind the barrels leading somewhere further.
help.cellar_key.thanks: My saviour! Here's the key. Just take a lamp — it's dark as the inside of a barrel down there.

help.tower_key.giver_name: Matvii Honchar, head of the community
help.tower_key.title: A Party by the Tower
help.tower_key.text: The water tower is a hundred years old! At the party I'd like to read something lovely and give flowers to our oldest resident. Bring a book from the library and a bouquet — and I'll trust you with the key to the tower. You can see the whole town from its platform.
help.tower_key.thanks: On behalf of the whole town — thank you! The key is yours. Just please don't climb onto the tank.

help.wool_1.title: The First Shearing
help.wool_1.text: The sheep need shearing before the heat, but my hands are full of cheese. Bring four handfuls of wool from the farm — and I'll teach you to spin.
help.wool_1.thanks: Good wool! Here are some mittens — made from your own wool, as it happens.

help.wool_2.title: Yarn for the Fair
help.wool_2.text: We need yarn for the fair — three skeins. The wheel's over there, the wool's at the farm. Can you manage?
help.wool_2.thanks: So even, you'd think a machine made it! Have a scarf — it's windy around here.

help.backpack.title: A Backpack for a Traveller
help.backpack.text: You carry so much back and forth, you need a proper backpack. Bring two wheels of your cheese and a jar of honey — I'll sell them at the fair, and with the takings I'll sew you a backpack from sturdy woollen cloth.
help.backpack.thanks: Here! Twenty little pockets for twenty adventures.

help.baker.title: Flour for the Harvest Festival
help.baker.text: The mill has stopped, and I need to bake loaves for the harvest festival. Three little sacks of flour — and I'm in your debt!
help.baker.thanks: There'll be a festive loaf for the whole town! And this pie is for you, still hot.

help.librarian.title: A Sky for the Reading Room
help.librarian.text: I'd like to decorate the reading room with a map of the sky. Sketch the stars through the telescope on the square and bring me a feather — we'll label the constellations in old ink.
help.librarian.thanks: Now the children will read under the stars. Thank you!

help.kitten.title: The Kitten by the Vet's
help.kitten.text: There's a kitten sitting by the vet clinic, so skinny! The vet says it needs feeding. Will you bring some milk and a fish? Pretty please!
help.kitten.thanks: It ate and fell asleep! I'll call it Little Rift. Have my charm — for luck.

help.radio.title: The Morning Show
help.radio.text: I'm on air at six in the morning, and the studio coffee machine has broken. Two coffees to go — and I'll give you a signed record!
help.radio.thanks: Good morning, Lypove! …Just practising for the show. Thank you!

help.farm.title: Winter Stores
help.farm.text: In winter the animals need lots of hay, and I can't keep up on my own. Three armfuls of hay and a jug of water — and I'll share some honey from my hives.
help.farm.thanks: The cows bow to you. Well, they're chewing, but it's the same thing.

help.church_flowers.title: Flowers for the Church Feast
help.church_flowers.text: For St Nicholas's Day I decorate the church. Two bouquets — and the altar will shine.
help.church_flowers.thanks: How beautiful! Father Mykhailo said it's the loveliest altar in ten years.

help.newsroom.title: The Postcard Contest
help.newsroom.text: The paper is holding a contest: “Lypove in Postcards”. Bring two postcards from the town hall — we'll print the best ones on the front page.
help.newsroom.thanks: Wonderful! One of them will go in the Sunday issue.

help.stable.title: Carrots for Burevii
help.stable.text: Burevii gets nervous before a race and only carrots calm him down. Three carrots and an armful of hay — and I'll show you the inside of the stables.
help.stable.thanks: Burevii will remember you. Have a horseshoe from his hoof — a real one, for luck.

0.q: What do you like most about Lypove?

answers.0: Morning coffee and the lindens on the square
answers.1: The people — everyone says hello here
answers.3: The bakery. Honestly, just the bakery

answers.1: Summer, for the river and wild strawberries

2.q: Do you believe the crystals in the cave sing?

answers.0: I've heard them with my own ears!
answers.1: It's the wind in the cracks
answers.2: I want to check for myself

3.q: What would you change about the town?

answers.2: Nothing — leave it as it is

4.q: Your recipe for a perfect day off?

5.q: Who do you think bakes the best bread?

answers.2: Me — I just haven't tried yet

6.q: What would you say to a cat asleep on your bench?

answers.0: I shuffle over and sit beside it
answers.1: I offer it a bit of fish
answers.3: I take its picture for the paper

7.q: What song would you request on “Lypove FM”?

answers.1: An old one, like when I was little
answers.3: A lullaby for the whole town

8.q: What does home mean to you?

answers.1: The smell of tea in the kitchen

9.q: Have you seen the golden fish in the pond?

answers.0: I have, but I won't tell you my wish
answers.1: No, but I believe in it
answers.2: I saw a catfish — does that count?
answers.3: I caught it and let it go

answers.1: Go out to the field at dawn
answers.2: Don't feed the cat from the bar — he's a sly one
