rc.pancakes.name: Pancakes with sour cream
rc.pancakes.text: Thin, with lacy edges: the first one comes out lumpy, of course.

rc.baked_potato.name: Baked potatoes
rc.baked_potato.text: Baked till the crust turns golden, with a knob of butter.

rc.syrnyky.name: Syrnyky
rc.syrnyky.text: Golden, soft inside, with a spoonful of jam.

rc.varenyky.name: Potato varenyky
rc.varenyky.text: You shape the next batch while the last one boils: that's how the evening goes by.

rc.borshch.name: Borscht
rc.borshch.text: Red, thick, with garlic — Granny's recipe.

rc.fish_soup.name: Fish soup
rc.fish_soup.text: Fish soup just like on the bank of the pond, only at home.

rc.mushroom_soup.name: Mushroom soup
rc.mushroom_soup.text: The smell of the forest fills the whole kitchen.

rc.corn_porridge.name: Cornmeal porridge
rc.corn_porridge.text: Cornmeal porridge with milk and butter — warmth from the inside.

rc.honey_cake.name: Honey cake
rc.honey_cake.text: Honey layers and sour-cream frosting: just the thing with tea.

rc.compote.name: Kompot
rc.compote.text: Berries, water and a little sugar: summer in a jug.

rc.herbal_tea.name: Chamomile tea
rc.herbal_tea.text: Camomile brewed with well water — and you can rest.

rc.kutia.name: Kutia
rc.kutia.text: Wheat, poppy seeds and honey — the main dish of Christmas Eve, the way Granny Zlata taught.

rc.uzvar.name: Uzvar
rc.uzvar.text: Dried fruit, water and a spoonful of honey: the smell of Christmas Eve.

rc.paska.name: Easter bread
rc.paska.text: Tall, glazed and sprinkled — Ostap showed how to keep it from sinking.

rc.kalach.name: Kalach
rc.kalach.text: Braided, as for an evening party: Sofiia plaits dough the way others plait hair.

rc.cherry_varenyky.name: Cherry varenyky
rc.cherry_varenyky.text: Cherries with stones or without — every family has its own truth.

rc.salad.name: Summer salad
rc.salad.text: Tomatoes, cucumber, dill and a pinch of salt — the taste of summer from your own garden.

rc.strawberry_jam.name: Strawberry jam
rc.strawberry_jam.text: Berries and sugar, a low flame, and the foam you're dying to lick off the spoon.

rc.pumpkin_porridge.name: Pumpkin porridge
rc.pumpkin_porridge.text: Sweet, orange, with butter — like Granny's in autumn.

cal.new_year_visit.title: New Year Treats for Granny Zlata
cal.new_year_visit.intro: Granny Zlata Koval couldn't bake anything sweet this year — her hands hurt. “If only I had a bit of honey cake for my tea, like in the old days…”

0.text: Bake a honey cake at home
0.done: The layers came out even, the cream just like Granny Zlata's used to be.

1.text: Take the honey cake to Granny Zlata
1.done: Granny Zlata clasped her hands and put the kettle on straight away.

cal.new_year_visit.bye: “Oh, child, you've made my holiday. Here, take these mittens — I knitted them back in autumn.”

cal.vodokhreshche.title: Holy Water for Liudmyla
cal.vodokhreshche.intro: Father Pavlo asks a favour: Granny Liudmyla Melnyk can't make it to church for Epiphany, but she'd dearly love some holy water.

0.text: Go to the blessing of the water at the church in the morning
0.done: The water is ice-cold, but the church is warm with candles.

1.text: Take the holy water to Granny Liudmyla
1.done: Liudmyla crossed herself and wept for joy.

cal.vodokhreshche.bye: Father Pavlo shook your hand: “A kind heart is the best prayer.”

cal.winter_firewood.title: Firewood for Oleh Oliinyk
cal.winter_firewood.intro: Grandpa Oleh has run out of firewood — the frost is hard, and he's not as strong as he was. The sawmill in the woods gives offcuts away for free.

0.text: Ask for offcuts at the sawmill in the woods
0.done: The sawyers tied up two bundles for you.

1.text: Take the firewood to Grandpa Oleh
1.done: At once the house smelled of resin.

cal.winter_firewood.bye: “Now I'll last till spring. Thank you for not forgetting an old man.”

cal.ice_fishing.title: Winter Fish Soup for Grandpa Petro
cal.ice_fishing.intro: Grandpa Petro Petrenko went ice fishing for forty winters, but now his legs won't let him. “If only I had some soup from our own fish…”

0.text: Catch fish in the village pond

1.text: Cook fish soup at home

2.text: Take the soup to Grandpa Petro
2.done: Grandpa took a taste and fell silent — he just kept nodding.

cal.ice_fishing.bye: “Just like at the pond with my own grandpa. Take this horseshoe — it used to bring me luck.”

cal.winter_reading.title: Winter Readings at the Library
cal.winter_reading.intro: Nataliia Honchar is gathering people for winter readings: whoever reads a book tells everyone about it at an evening get-together.

0.text: Borrow a book from the library

1.text: Read at home for a few evenings

2.text: What will you say about the book at the reading?

0.label: “I cried over the last pages”
0.text: Nataliia smiled quietly: “Then it's alive.”

1.label: “I laughed so hard the whole house heard”
1.text: The room laughed along with you.

cal.winter_reading.bye: “Come again. Books get lonely on the shelves.”

cal.valentine_letter.title: A Letter for Orest
cal.valentine_letter.intro: Sofiia Kravets blushes and holds out an envelope: “Give this to Orest Sydorenko… just don't say who it's from. Although… well, as you like.”

0.text: What will you do with the letter?

0.label: Give it to Orest, as asked
0.text: Orest turned the envelope over and over in his hands, smiling.

1.label: Tell Sofiia: “Tell him yourself”
1.text: Sofiia sighed… and went to him herself. An hour later they were seen together by the fountain.
Give the letter to Orest Sydorenko
1.done: Orest read it and went off to buy flowers.

2.text: Take a look at the square in the evening
2.done: By the fountain, two people are holding hands. Looks like you saw it right.

cal.valentine_letter.bye: Sofiia winks at you over Orest's shoulder.

cal.maslyana.title: Pancakes for Maslyana
cal.maslyana.intro: Granny Zlata Melnyk says Maslyana without pancakes is like spring without sun. And she's run out of flour.

0.text: Make pancakes at home

1.text: Treat Granny Zlata to pancakes
1.done: “So thin! And was the first one lumpy? Good — that's how it should be.”

cal.maslyana.bye: “Farewell, winter. Take a jar of jam — for the pancakes.”

cal.frozen_pipe.title: Water While the Pipe Is Fixed
cal.frozen_pipe.intro: Zlata Rudenko from the council works: a pipe has frozen on the street, and while it's being mended people need water.

0.text: Draw water from the well at the farm

1.text: Take the water to the office
1.done: Zlata wrote you down in the “Who Helped” notebook. Mind you, no one has ever seen this notebook.

cal.frozen_pipe.bye: “The pipe's thawed. Lypove holds together when people hold together.”

cal.winter_cats.title: Hungry Cats in Winter
cal.winter_cats.intro: Sviatoslav Lysenko the vet is worried: in the frost, the stray cats can't find any food.

0.text: Catch a fish

1.text: Feed the cat by the vet clinic

cal.winter_cats.bye: “The ginger one even let me stroke him. That's a victory.”

cal.snowman.title: A Snowman by the School
cal.snowman.intro: Orest Savchuk has taken his class out into the schoolyard: “Who'll show us how to build a proper snowman?”

0.text: Come to the schoolyard after lessons

1.text: What kind of snowman will it be?

0.label: With a carrot and a bucket, the proper way
0.text: The children bring a carrot from home and a bucket from the storeroom.

1.label: An astronaut snowman
1.text: The bucket becomes a helmet and the twigs become antennas. The teacher takes a photo for the paper.

cal.snowman.bye: For a whole week the children wave to you from the classroom window.

cal.march_eighth.title: Flowers for Granny Zlata from Grandpa Vasyl
cal.march_eighth.intro: Grandpa Vasyl Koval whispers: “For fifty years I've given her flowers. But this time my legs won't carry me to the flower shop…”

0.text: Buy a bouquet at the “Pivonia” flower shop

1.text: Give the bouquet to Grandpa Vasyl
1.done: Grandpa hid the bouquet behind his back and set off home, as if to a first date.

cal.march_eighth.bye: In the evening Granny Zlata tells the whole street what a husband she has.

cal.spring_cleanup.title: Spring Clean-up at the Scrapyard
cal.spring_cleanup.intro: Mykola Shevchenko from the scrapyard: the melting snow has turned up lots of good junk. Maybe some of it can still be useful?

0.text: Look for something worthwhile at the scrapyard

1.text: Take your find to the “Second Life” workshop
1.done: Viktoriia Rudenko looked it over: “It's got life in it yet!”

cal.spring_cleanup.bye: “See — not everything lying at the scrapyard is rubbish.”

cal.birdhouses.title: Birdhouses for the School
cal.birdhouses.intro: Zoriana Lytvyn the forester: the starlings are already on their way, and there are hardly any birdhouses. The schoolchildren will make some if they have boards.

0.text: Ask for boards at the sawmill
0.done: The sawyers picked out some straight boards.

1.text: Take the boards to the school
1.done: A week later, every linden by the school has a birdhouse.

cal.birdhouses.bye: Zoriana says the starlings are singing louder this spring. Maybe they really are.

cal.palm_sunday.title: A Willow Sprig for Granny Liudmyla
cal.palm_sunday.intro: Palm Sunday. Granny Liudmyla Melnyk is sad she can't get to church to have her willow blessed.

0.text: Come to the church for the blessing
0.done: The priest sprinkles the willow, and the children laugh at the cold drops.

1.text: Take the willow to Granny Liudmyla
1.done: “It's not me tapping you — it's the willow!” laughs Granny, touching you lightly with the sprig.

cal.palm_sunday.bye: Easter is a week away — Granny Liudmyla is already counting the days.

cal.sowing_seeds.title: Seeds for the Garden
cal.sowing_seeds.intro: Ostap Petrenko from the farm is going to sow sunflowers along the edge of the field. The seeds are at the market, and he's busy with the tractor.

0.text: Buy sunflower seeds at the market

1.text: Take the seeds to the farm
1.done: Ostap poured the seeds into the seed drill.

cal.sowing_seeds.bye: “By autumn half the field will be gold. Come and see.”

cal.pysanky.title: Easter Eggs
cal.pysanky.intro: Every year Granny Zlata Koval paints pysanky — Easter eggs — for the whole street. This year she's short of eggs.

0.text: Collect eggs at the farm

1.text: Take the eggs to Granny Zlata
1.done: Granny is already melting the wax.

2.text: What will you do with the pysanka?

0.label: Keep it
0.text: The pysanka goes on the shelf — until next Easter.

1.label: Take it to the church, to the basket for people living alone
1.text: Father Pavlo put it in the basket labelled “From the Neighbours”.

cal.pysanky.bye: “And I'll teach you to bake paska. No, not me — Ostap from the bakery. Tell him I sent you.”

cal.paska.title: Paska with Ostap
cal.paska.intro: Ostap Sydorenko the baker: “Granny Zlata says I should teach you? I will. Only dough doesn't like haste or draughts.”

0.text: Listen to Ostap

0.label: Listen closely and take notes
0.text: You write down: “don't open the oven, don't slam the doors.”

1.text: Bake paska at home

2.text: Show the paska to Ostap
2.done: Ostap tapped the crust and nodded: “You're one of us.”

cal.paska.bye: “Christ is risen! Now you're a baker too — a little bit.”

cal.first_garden.title: The First Garden Bed
cal.first_garden.intro: Oleksandra Sydorenko is digging her garden and calls for help: “Hands in the soil — and spring is yours.”

0.text: Come to the farm in the morning
0.done: The earth smells so good you almost want to eat it. Almost.

1.text: Feed the animals while Oleksandra hoes

cal.first_garden.bye: “In autumn I'll bring you some carrots. That's a promise, not a thank-you.”

cal.chamomile_tea.title: Camomile Tea for the Hospital
cal.chamomile_tea.intro: Nurse Lidiia Diachuk: “Camomile tea is the best thing for patients, and the pharmacy stuff just isn't the same.”

0.text: Pick camomile in the field

1.text: Draw water from the well

2.text: Brew the tea at home

3.text: Take the tea to the hospital
3.done: The ward smelled of the field.

cal.chamomile_tea.bye: “You see — nobody minds taking their medicine when there's tea.”

cal.provody.title: Remembrance Day at the Cemetery
cal.provody.intro: A week after Easter. The caretaker, Roman Sydorenko, is tidying the cemetery — all of Lypove will come for the day of remembrance.

0.text: Buy a bouquet

1.text: Lay flowers on the old, forgotten graves

cal.provody.bye: “Here lie those whom nobody visits any more. Thank you for remembering them.”

cal.toloka.title: A Working Bee in the Park
cal.toloka.intro: Matvii Honchar, head of the community, is calling everyone to a working bee: to mend the park benches before summer.

0.text: Pick up boards at the sawmill
0.done: The sawyers know about the working bee.

1.text: Bring the boards to the square
1.done: The benches creak in a new way now — a cheerful one.

cal.toloka.bye: Matvii puts up a notice on the board: “Thank you to everyone who came.” Your name is there too.

cal.remembrance.title: A Candle of Remembrance
cal.remembrance.intro: The eighth of May. Father Pavlo asks you to light a candle for those who didn't come back.

0.text: Light a candle in the church

1.text: Buy flowers

2.text: Lay flowers at the cemetery

cal.remembrance.bye: The cemetery is especially quiet today.

cal.swarm.title: A Swarm in the Apple Tree
cal.swarm.intro: Bohdan Shevchenko comes running across the field: “The bees have swarmed! They've settled on the old apple tree — help me before they fly off!”

0.text: Run to the apple tree at the farm

1.text: What will you do with the swarm?

0.label: Hold the ladder while Bohdan shakes the swarm into a skep
0.text: The swarm buzzes, but pours obediently into the skep.

1.label: Call the beekeeper next door
1.text: The neighbour hurried over with his smoker and calmly took care of everything. Bohdan treated you both to honey.

cal.swarm.bye: “Now I've got one more hive. I'll share the honey — just remind me.”

cal.exam_books.title: Books for the Exams
cal.exam_books.intro: Ivan Rudenko: “Exams are just around the corner, and the class is short of textbooks. The library has some, but who's going to fetch them…”

0.text: Borrow a book from the library

1.text: Take a book to the classroom
1.done: The pupils pass the book from hand to hand like treasure.

cal.exam_books.bye: “If they pass, they'll thank you too. I certainly will.”

cal.lilac.title: Wildflowers for the Shop Window
cal.lilac.intro: Petro Diachuk the florist wants a window display of wildflowers: “So people walk by and smile.”

0.text: Pick flowers in the field

1.text: Bring the flowers to “Pivonia”
1.done: Petro puts the flowers in an old jug in the middle of the window.

cal.lilac.bye: Passers-by really do stop at the window.

cal.childrens_day.title: Sweets for Children's Day
cal.childrens_day.intro: The first of June. There's a children's party on the square, and there aren't enough buns for the little ones.

0.text: Buy a bun at the stall

1.text: Take the sweets to the children on the square
1.done: The children share one bun between six — and there's enough for everyone.

cal.childrens_day.bye: One of the little ones draws you in chalk on the cobbles. It's a good likeness.

cal.trinity.title: Greenery for Trinity
cal.trinity.intro: Granny Zlata Melnyk: “For the Green Holidays we decorate the house with branches and herbs, but I can't make it to the woods.”

0.text: Gather herbs and branches in the woods
0.done: Linden, maple, thyme, lovage — it smells like childhood.

1.text: Take the greenery to Granny Zlata
1.done: Granny lays the herbs on the windowsill and under the threshold.

cal.trinity.bye: “Now the house is blessed. And so are you — a little.”

cal.kupala.title: A Kupala wreath
cal.kupala.intro: Sofiia Kravets: “Shall we weave wreaths and float them on the pond? Whoever's floats furthest will be lucky!”

0.text: Pick wildflowers

1.text: Weave a wreath with Sofiia on the square
1.done: Your fingers won't cooperate, but Sofiia helps.

2.text: What will you do with the wreath?

0.label: Float it on the pond
0.text: The wreath floats far, far away, past the reeds. Sofiia claps her hands.

1.label: Give it to Sofiia
1.text: For some reason Sofiia blushes and puts the wreath on.

cal.kupala.bye: They sing over the pond until morning.

cal.haymaking.title: Haymaking
cal.haymaking.intro: Tetiana Shevchenko from the field: “The hay's drying, and rain is on the way. Every pair of hands is worth its weight in gold.”

0.text: Gather hay at the farm

1.text: Help build a haystack in the field
1.done: The haystack comes out a bit crooked, but sturdy.

cal.haymaking.bye: “We made it! Now let it pour.”

cal.constitution_concert.title: A Concert on the Radio
cal.constitution_concert.intro: Oleh Bondar from “Lypove FM” is doing a holiday show and looking for someone to request a song for all of Lypove.

0.text: Come to the radio station in the evening

1.text: Request a song for everyone

cal.constitution_concert.bye: Your song plays from every window.

cal.statehood_flags.title: Flags on the Square
cal.statehood_flags.intro: Matvii Honchar is getting the square ready for Statehood Day: there are plenty of flags, but no hands.

0.text: Pick up the flags at the town hall
0.done: A whole armful of blue-and-yellow flags.

1.text: Hang the flags on the square
1.done: At once the square looks festive.

cal.statehood_flags.bye: Matvii takes a photo of the square: “For history.”

cal.cherry_varenyky.title: Cherry varenyky
cal.cherry_varenyky.intro: The cherries in Zlata Koval's garden are falling, and her grandchildren are far away. “Want me to teach you to make varenyky? Just pick the cherries.”

0.text: Pick cherries in the garden

1.text: Learn from Granny Zlata

0.label: Shape them together with Granny
0.text: The first varenyky fall apart; the seventh comes out just like hers.

2.text: Make varenyky at home

cal.cherry_varenyky.bye: Granny Zlata tells everyone she has an apprentice now.

cal.dawn_fishing.title: Fishing at dawn
cal.dawn_fishing.intro: Myron: “They bite best at dawn. Coming? Whoever catches more is the braver one.”

0.text: Come to the pond at dawn
0.done: Mist over the water. Myron is silent — you don't talk here.

1.text: Catch a fish

cal.dawn_fishing.bye: Myron caught more. But yours is bigger. So he says.

cal.starfall.title: Shooting Stars
cal.starfall.intro: Yurii Petrenko the photographer: “The Perseids! I want a sky map for the paper — who'll draw it while I set up the camera?”

0.text: Sketch the stars at the telescope on the square

1.text: Take the star map to the newspaper office
1.done: Yurii puts your map next to his photo.

cal.starfall.bye: In Thursday's issue there's a spread: “Shooting Stars over Lypove”. Your name is in small print at the bottom.

cal.harvest_flour.title: The First Flour of the New Harvest
cal.harvest_flour.intro: Iryna Koval: “The new wheat is in! Whoever mills it first gets the first palianytsia from the baker.”

0.text: Reap wheat

1.text: Gather more ears of wheat at the edge of the field

2.text: Mill the flour at the bread factory

3.text: Take the flour to the bakery
3.done: Ostap smells of fresh bread even from a distance.

cal.harvest_flour.bye: The first palianytsia of the new harvest is yours. Ostap said so, and there's no arguing with him.

cal.honey_spas.title: Honey Saviour's Day
cal.honey_spas.intro: Bohdan Shevchenko: “The first honey gets blessed. Bring yours too.”

0.text: Collect honey at the farm

1.text: Take the honey to the church to be blessed
1.done: The priest sprinkles the honey, and bees circle over the baskets.

cal.honey_spas.bye: Honey tastes sweeter after the feast. Or does it just seem so?

cal.apple_spas.title: Apple Saviour's Day
cal.apple_spas.intro: Father Pavlo: “Before the Saviour's Day we don't eat apples. Afterwards, we take the blessed ones to those who couldn't come.”

0.text: Pick apples in the orchard

1.text: Bring the apples to be blessed
1.done: The apples in the basket glow like little lanterns.

2.text: Take the blessed apples to Granny Liudmyla
2.done: “The first apple is for those who are no longer with us.”

cal.apple_spas.bye: Father Pavlo smiles: “Now it's a real feast.”

cal.independence_issue.title: The Holiday Issue
cal.independence_issue.intro: Nina Oliinyk the editor: “We need a photo of the square on Independence Day. Our photographer is ill — help us out!”

0.text: Photograph the square during the day
0.done: Flags, embroidered shirts, children on their parents' shoulders — click!

1.text: Take the photo to the newspaper office
1.done: Nina looks at the photo for a long, long time.

cal.independence_issue.bye: Your photo is on the front page. The caption reads: “Photo: a friend of the paper.”

cal.school_ready.title: The School Before the First of September
cal.school_ready.intro: Petro Rudenko: “The desks have gone wobbly, and there's no money for new ones. If I had some boards, I'd fix them.”

0.text: Ask for boards at the sawmill
0.done: The sawyers already know what they're for.

1.text: Bring the boards to the school
1.done: Petro is already there with a hammer and nails between his teeth.

cal.school_ready.bye: On the first of September the children sit down at desks that don't wobble.

cal.corn_market.title: Corn for the Fair
cal.corn_market.intro: Daryna Rudenko from the market: “Boiled corn is the hit of August. Bring a few cobs from the farm!”

0.text: Pick corn at the farm

1.text: Bring the corn to the market
1.done: Daryna puts a pot on the fire.

cal.corn_market.bye: By evening the market smells of boiled corn and salt.

cal.first_september.title: A Bouquet for the First of September
cal.first_september.intro: Little Ostap Savchuk is starting first grade, and his mum is on shift at the fire station. The teacher asks: “Let the boy have a bouquet too.”

0.text: Buy a bouquet at “Pivonia”

1.text: Give the bouquet to little Ostap by the school
1.done: Little Ostap holds the bouquet with both hands, as if it's the most important thing in his life.

cal.first_september.bye: The first-grader waves to you from the school assembly. The bouquet is bigger than he is.

cal.first_porcini.title: The First Porcini
cal.first_porcini.intro: Zoriana the forester: “The porcini are up! Just don't pull them out by the roots, and leave the fly agarics alone.”

0.text: Find a porcini mushroom in the woods

1.text: Sell the mushrooms at the shop
1.done: The shopkeeper weighs the mushroom and shows it to her neighbour: “What a beauty!”

cal.first_porcini.bye: Zoriana says it's a good sign: it'll be a mushroom autumn.

cal.harvest_fair.title: The Autumn Fair
cal.harvest_fair.intro: Daryna Rudenko is collecting vegetables for the autumn fair: “The best of the harvest goes in the front row!”

0.text: Pick corn

1.text: Buy carrots at the stall so you don't arrive empty-handed

2.text: Bring the vegetables to the market
2.done: The row of vegetables on the counter looks like an exhibition.

cal.harvest_fair.bye: The fair bustles until evening. Someone's already asking whose corn it is.

cal.warm_socks.title: Warm Mittens for Winter
cal.warm_socks.intro: Uliana Koval the weaver: “I'd like to knit mittens for the kindergarten before winter. If only I had some wool…”

0.text: Shear a sheep at the farm

1.text: Spin yarn at “Ovechka”

2.text: Give the yarn to Uliana
2.done: Uliana is already trying out her knitting needles.

cal.warm_socks.bye: A week later all the little ones at the kindergarten are wearing matching mittens.

cal.class_shelf.title: A Bookshelf for the Classroom
cal.class_shelf.intro: Nataliia Honchar: “The first grade hasn't got a single book. Take them this one — from the library.”

0.text: Borrow a book from the library

1.text: Take the book to the classroom
1.done: The children place the book on the empty shelf as solemnly as a Christmas tree.

cal.class_shelf.bye: The shelf isn't empty any more. It's a start.

cal.defenders.title: Postcards for the Defenders
cal.defenders.intro: Oksana Shevchenko from the post office is collecting postcards for the men and women at the front: “A few warm words mean a lot.”

0.text: Buy a postcard with a view of Lypove at the town hall

1.text: Take the postcard to the post office
1.done: Hryhorii stamps it carefully, as if it were an official document.

cal.defenders.bye: A month later the paper prints a reply: “Thank you, Lypove. Expect us.”

cal.pokrova_fair.title: The Pokrova Fair
cal.pokrova_fair.intro: Matvii Honchar: at Pokrova there's a fair, and every household brings something. “Apples or pears would be nice — something to treat people with.”

0.text: Pick apples or pears in the orchard

1.text: Bring the fruit to the square
1.done: Your pears sit on the table next to the pies.

cal.pokrova_fair.bye: The fair was a success. Matvii even danced — for the first time in ten years.

cal.scary_stories.title: Scary Stories at the Library
cal.scary_stories.intro: Before Halloween, Nataliia Honchar hosts an evening of scary stories by candlelight.

0.text: Come to the library in the evening

1.text: Which story will you tell?

0.label: The miner who still walks the cave
0.text: The children huddled together, and Grandpa Panas grumbled: “Nonsense! He doesn't walk. He sits.”

1.label: The cat who reads the newspapers
1.text: Everyone laughed, even the ones who had meant to be scared.

cal.scary_stories.bye: Nataliia blows out the candles: “Until next year. If we survive, ha-ha.”

cal.autumn_firewood.title: Firewood Before the Cold
cal.autumn_firewood.intro: Grandpa Oleh Oliinyk counts his logs and shakes his head: “It won't last till spring.”

0.text: Ask for firewood at the sawmill
0.done: Two bundles, tied with wire.

1.text: Stack the wood at Grandpa Oleh's
1.done: Grandpa stacks the logs neatly, like bricks.

cal.class_hike.title: A Class Trip to the Forest
cal.class_hike.intro: Autumn break. Ivan Rudenko is taking his class to the forest and needs one more grown-up.

0.text: Come to the forest in the morning
0.done: The children scatter like sparrows.

1.text: Show the children where mushrooms and berries grow

cal.class_hike.bye: In the evening the children tell their parents they saw a real woodpecker. And you.

cal.andrew_eve.title: St Andrew's Eve Party
cal.andrew_eve.intro: Sofiia Kravets invites you to the evening party: “The kalyta, fortune-telling, songs! Only someone has to bake the kalach for the kalyta…”

0.text: Sofiia shows you how to braid a kalach

0.label: Braid it together
0.text: The dough stretches like a plait. It's working!

1.text: Bake a kalach at home

2.text: Bring the kalach to the party
2.done: The kalach is hung on a red ribbon. Bite it without your hands — and don't laugh!

0.label: Pour wax into water
0.text: The wax sets into the shape of… a boat? A journey, the girls say.

1.label: Count the stakes in the fence
1.text: An even number! Sofiia winks.

cal.andrew_eve.bye: The party ends near dawn. The songs carry down the street for a long while.

cal.scarves_for_kids.title: Scarves for the Kindergarten
cal.scarves_for_kids.intro: Uliana Koval: “We have mittens, but no scarves. With yarn for just one, I'd still make it before the frosts.”

0.text: Shear a sheep

1.text: Spin yarn

2.text: Weave a scarf

3.done: Uliana holds the scarf to her cheek: “So soft.”

cal.scarves_for_kids.bye: At the kindergarten the scarf went to the littlest one. He won't take it off even indoors.

cal.window_wool.title: Seal Granny Zlata's Windows
cal.window_wool.intro: Granny Zlata Koval: “There's such a draught from the windows a candle won't stay lit. If only I had wool to stuff the gaps, like we used to.”

0.text: Shear a sheep at the farm

1.text: Take the wool to Granny Zlata
1.done: Together you stuff the gaps while Granny tells you about her youth.

cal.window_wool.bye: “Now it's warm. And I still have plenty of stories to tell you.”

cal.hospital_soup.title: Something Hot for the Hospital
cal.hospital_soup.intro: Doctor Taras Melnyk: “November means flu. The patients could use something hot and homemade, not canteen food.”

0.text: Cook borscht at home

1.text: Bring the hot food to the hospital
1.done: Someone on the ward asked for seconds for the first time in a week.

cal.hospital_soup.bye: “There's a medicine you won't find at the pharmacy.”

cal.bird_feeder.title: A Bird Feeder for Winter
cal.bird_feeder.intro: Zoriana the forester: “The tits have already come to the houses. Put out some seeds and they'll sing for you till spring.”

0.text: Buy sunflower seeds

1.text: Fill the bird feeder on the square

cal.bird_feeder.bye: In the morning there's a little tit on the windowsill. Waiting.

cal.st_nicholas.title: St Nicholas's Helper
cal.st_nicholas.intro: Father Pavlo: “Nicholas can't get to everyone. Deliver the presents to the children — quietly, so they don't see.”

0.text: Leave a present by Petryk Melnyk's door
0.done: Quiet as snow.

1.text: Leave a present at the school for the class
1.done: The teacher hides the present in the cupboard until morning.

2.text: Leave a present by Hannusia Lysenko's door
2.done: A dog barked somewhere — quick, away from here!

cal.st_nicholas.bye: In the morning all of Lypove writes to the paper that St Nicholas was especially generous this year.

cal.kutia.title: Kutia for Christmas Eve
cal.kutia.intro: Granny Zlata Melnyk: “Without kutia, supper isn't a feast. I'll teach you — write it down, nobody knows how anymore.”

0.text: Listen to Granny Zlata

0.label: Write down every word
0.text: “The wheat soaks overnight. The poppy seeds — grind them till the milk runs white. Honey goes in last.”

1.text: Buy wheat at the holiday market

2.text: Buy poppy seeds

5.text: Bring the kutia to Granny Zlata
5.done: Granny tastes it and silently wipes her eyes.

cal.kutia.bye: “Now there's someone to pass it on to. Christ is born!”

cal.uzvar.title: Uzvar for Grandpa Vasyl
cal.uzvar.intro: Grandpa Vasyl Koval: “Zlata makes the kutia, but the uzvar was always mine. This year my hands shake… I'll show you how, and you'll cook it?”

0.text: Listen to Grandpa Vasyl

0.label: Listen and nod
0.text: “Dried fruit, water, honey — and don't rush anything.”

1.text: Buy dried fruit at the fair

2.text: Draw water from the well

5.text: Bring the uzvar to Grandpa Vasyl
5.done: Grandpa pours two mugs — one for you, one for him.

cal.uzvar.bye: “There we go. Now it's a holiday for me too.”

cal.carols.title: Carollers
cal.carols.intro: Oleh Bondar is gathering carollers: “We'll go round the village and then sing on air! Will you carry the star?”

0.text: Come to the square in the evening with the star
0.done: The star glows, the snow crunches, someone sings off-key — and it's wonderful.

1.text: Which carol will you sing by the town hall?

0.label: “Good evening to you, master of the house”
0.text: Matvii Honchar comes out onto the porch and treats everyone to kalach.

1.label: “Shchedryk”
1.text: Even Grandpa Panas joins in. Quietly, but he joins in.

2.text: Sing on the radio
2.done: Now all of Lypove can hear you.

cal.carols.bye: They let you keep the star as a keepsake.

cal.square_tree.title: A Fir Tree for the Square
cal.square_tree.intro: Matvii Honchar: “The forester said we could take one fir from the thinning. Which one is up to you — I trust you.”

0.text: Pick a fir in the forest with the forester

1.text: Which tree will you take?

0.label: A tall, slender one
0.text: It barely fits on the trailer.

1.label: A fluffy one, even if a bit crooked
1.text: “It's got soul, though,” says Zoriana.

2.text: Decorate the tree on the square
2.done: Ornaments from the school's craft lessons, a garland from the town hall. The best tree in a hundred years.

cal.square_tree.bye: In the evening the lights go on. All of Lypove counts down: “Three, two, one!”

cal.new_year_eve.title: Gingerbread for New Year's Eve
cal.new_year_eve.intro: Dmytro Shevchenko the baker: “It's New Year's Eve and there's hardly any gingerbread for the square. It was all gone before lunch!”

0.text: Buy a pie at the bakery

1.text: Bring something sweet to the square before midnight
1.done: The pie is cut into thirty slices. There's enough for everyone. A miracle.

cal.new_year_eve.bye: At midnight fireworks burst over the square, and someone shouts your name along with “Happy New Year!”

first.home.title: A letter on the table
first.home.intro:
Good morning, neighbour! It's me, Granny Zlata from the house across the road. You've found the key already, so let me tell you how to live here.

You go wherever you like: slide your finger on the circle at the bottom of the screen (on a computer — the arrows or WASD), or just touch the floor where you want to go. Walk up to a thing and the big button at the side says what to do with it: sit, lie down, cook, switch on. Or touch the thing itself.

The door to the street is the one with the porch. Walk up to it and press «Door» (or touch the door) — and you're outside. Home again the same way, through your own door: there's a green mark glowing on the ground by it. And when you want to move the furniture or paint the walls — the «Room» button at the top.

Go on, step outside, I'll write to you again.

0.text: Step out of the house
0.done: Outside it smells of linden and fresh bread. Granny Zlata waves from the bench across the road.

first.home.bye: “That's it! — calls Granny Zlata. — See, nothing to it. I'll leave you another letter.”

first.welcome.title: A letter about the board
first.welcome.intro:
Neighbour, it's me again. You've got a good house, only it doesn't like being forgotten. The fridge hums like an old cat — keep food in it, and cook on the stove: a bowl of soup keeps you warm even in a frost. The bed is by the window, the wardrobe with your clothes is in the corner, and the chest keeps whatever won't fit in your inventory. Once a month bills come for the power, water, gas and rubbish — take them to the utility office, or they'll switch things off without asking.

Now have a look around. By the market, across the road from the square, there's a notice board — people write there what they're short of. Read it: that's how folk in Lypove get to know each other.

0.text: Read the notice board by the market
0.done: On the board: a lost cat, a bicycle for sale and a working party by the school. Lypove feels closer at once.

first.welcome.bye: “There we are,” says Granny Zlata from her bench. “Now you're a little bit local.”

first.market.title: A letter about the market
first.market.intro:
Neighbour, it's me again. I saw you reading the board — well done.

Our market is across the road from the square: two rows of stalls, and everything's fresh. In town you earn money with your hands — at the post office, the bakery, the farm — but at home, however hard you try, no coins will come. Home is for cooking, planting and resting.

Buy a warm bun at the market — the baker always winks at new people. And in the morning there'll be a fresh newspaper by your door: everything that happened yesterday and what's coming tomorrow.

0.text: Buy a bun at the market
0.done: The bun is still warm, with poppy seeds. The baker winks: “The second one's tomorrow!”

first.market.bye: “Tasty?” Granny Zlata laughs. “Then you're one of us.”

first.seeds.title: A letter about the garden
first.seeds.intro:
Neighbour, there are beds behind your house — empty, it breaks my heart.

Seeds are sold at Kolosok and the hardware store, seedlings at Pivonia. Stand by a bed and it'll tell you what it needs: planting, watering or picking. Water every day when it doesn't rain, and twice in the heat. Carrots need a little time, like everything good.

Start with carrots: they forgive beginners.

0.text: Buy carrot seeds at Kolosok
0.done: The packet rustles in your pocket. The shopkeeper says to sow in rows.

first.seeds.bye: “Plant them today,” says Granny Zlata. “The earth likes to be remembered.”

first.cafe.title: A letter about people
first.cafe.intro:
Neighbour, this is my last letter; you'll manage on your own from here.

There's an old paper map in your pocket with all of Lypove on it: touch a name and it'll show you the way. If it's far or raining, call a taxi — only in the rain it costs more. Look for work among people: the post office, the bakery and the farm always need hands, and the notice board will tell you who's waiting for help.

Our people are kind, if a bit headstrong. Drop into the Lypa café and have a coffee — the whole town's news is there.

0.text: Have a coffee at Lypa
0.done: The barista draws a linden leaf in the foam. At the next table they argue about the weather and the power plant.

first.cafe.bye: “That's it,” Granny Zlata writes on a scrap of paper under the door. “Lypove is yours now. I bake pies on Saturdays — drop in.”

rift.ch1.title: The Glowing Seed
rift.ch1.intro: Granny Zlata stands by the rift with an empty flowerpot. “All my life I've dreamed of a glass roof and flowers taller than trees. If it's true — bring me something living from there.”

0.text: Step into the rift — into the Sunken Greenhouse
0.done: The water is ankle-deep and warm. Under the glass roof there's a hum like a beehive, and it smells of rain.

1.text: Find a glowing seed
1.done: The seed pulses in your palm like a tiny heart.

2.text: Take the seed to Granny Zlata
2.done: Granny Zlata plants it in the pot and can't take her eyes off it.

rift.ch1.bye: “So I didn't make it up. Let's see what grows from it — here, with me, in this world.”

reward.title: The one who saw the rift

rift.ch2.title: A Signal from the Desert
rift.ch2.intro: Oleh from the radio didn't sleep all night: “Someone is talking on an empty frequency. In your voice. Saying: ‘I'm in the white city, come.’ It's the solstice today — the rifts are open. Go and check, will you?”

0.text: Pass through the rift — to the Salt Sea
0.done: White all the way to the horizon. Salt crunches underfoot, and a city shimmers above the dunes.

1.text: The mirage city is getting closer. What do you do?

0.label: Walk into its square
0.text: The houses are see-through like soap bubbles. Someone has just left — the footprints in the sand are still warm. Yours.

1.label: Stand and watch from afar
1.text: The city sighs as if alive and drifts one step further away.

2.text: Pick up the glass shard with the mirage
2.done: In the shard you can see a square that isn't there. And someone waving.

3.done: Oleh holds the shard to the receiver — and the static falls silent.

rift.ch2.bye: “Silence… You took that voice with you. Maybe it's for the best.”

rift.ch3.title: A page from the future
rift.ch3.intro: Nataliia the librarian shows you a card from the catalogue: “We never had this book. But there's a card for it — dated tomorrow. It's the equinox today. Look over there, on the other side, where the books grow.”

0.text: Step into the rift — into the Clockwork Garden
0.done: Amber light. Every tree ticks, and pages fall from the branches instead of leaves.

1.text: Catch a page from the future
1.done: The ink is still wet. The text writes itself while you watch.

2.text: Take the page to Nataliia
2.done: Nataliia reads it aloud — and stops mid-word.

rift.ch3.bye: “It's about tomorrow. Nothing scary — just rain, and someone finally returning a book. I'll keep it in the catalogue under ‘Not Yet Written’.”

rift.ch4.title: Lypove Inside Out
rift.ch4.intro: Viktoriia the craftswoman turns a shard in her fingers: “On the longest night the rift leads into our own town — only it isn't people who live there. Nobody goes without a light. Bring me two shards and honey for wax, and I'll make you a lantern.”

0.text: Bring Viktoriia two shards and honey for wax
0.done: Viktoriia works in silence. The workshop fills with a light it has never known.

1.text: Walk with the lantern into Lypove Inside Out at dusk
1.done: The snow falls upwards. Someone peers out of your windows — with a lantern for a head.

2.text: A creature with a lantern for a head stops beside you and waits.

0.label: Raise your own lantern in reply
0.text: It bows its head — lantern to lantern — and walks on down your street, at your pace.

1.label: Stand still until it passes
1.text: It passes so close you can hear the fire crackling inside it.

3.text: Catch a snowflake that falls upwards
3.done: The snowflake in the jar just won't settle to the bottom.

rift.ch4.bye: “Now you know who lives in our town when we aren't looking. Look after the lantern — and look after Lypove, whichever side of it you're on.”

job.parcels.title: Parcels from the Post Office
job.parcels.text: {giver} from the post office can't keep up with the parcels: one for {t1}, another for {t2}.

0.text: Deliver a parcel: {t1}
0.done: They signed for it — and said thank you.

1.text: Deliver a parcel: {t2}
1.done: “Oh, it's from my sister!”

job.medicine.title: Medicine for {who}
job.medicine.text: {who} is ill. {giver} from the hospital asks you to take the medicine to their home — they can't go out themselves.

0.text: Bring the medicine: {who}
0.done: “Thank you… I feel better already, and I haven't even taken it.”

job.sick_soup.title: Something Hot for {who}
job.sick_soup.text: {who} is ill in bed, and there's nobody at home to cook. {giver} says: “A bowl of something homemade is the best medicine.”

0.text: Bring something hot: {who}
0.done: Spoonful by spoonful — and the colour comes back to their cheeks.

job.lost_kitten.title: A Lost Kitten
job.lost_kitten.text: {giver} is looking for a kitten: it ran off yesterday. Someone saw it near {place}.

0.text: Look for the kitten: {place}
0.done: Mewing from under the bushes! Trembling, but unhurt.

1.text: Bring the kitten back to its owners
1.done: The kitten climbs straight into their arms and purrs.

job.lost_puppy.title: A Runaway Puppy
job.lost_puppy.text: {giver} is in tears: the puppy slipped out through the gate. The neighbours saw it near {place}.

0.text: Look for the puppy: {place}
0.done: The puppy leaps happily into your lap.

1.text: Bring the puppy back
1.done: Its tail spins like a propeller.

job.firewood.title: Firewood for {giver}
job.firewood.text: {giver} is running out of firewood, and the sawmill gives offcuts away for free.

0.text: Get some offcuts at the sawmill
0.done: Two bundles.

1.text: Deliver the firewood
1.done: The stove in the house starts crackling.

job.fire_planks.title: Boards After the Fire
job.fire_planks.text: There was a fire yesterday: {place}. {giver} from the fire station is looking for someone to bring boards to patch the roof.

0.text: Ask for boards at the sawmill
0.done: The sawyers had already heard about the fire — they gave you their best.

1.text: Bring the boards to the burnt house
1.done: The roof was patched by evening.

job.harvest_hands.title: Hands for the Harvest
job.harvest_hands.text: {giver} from the field: “The rain's coming and the sheaves aren't tied!”

0.text: Reap wheat

1.text: Help tie the sheaves
1.done: The sheaves stand in a row like little soldiers.

job.library_return.title: The Forgotten Book
job.library_return.text: {giver} from the library: {t1} has had a book for three months now. Maybe you could remind them, as a neighbour?

0.text: Drop in on the neighbour: {t1}
0.done: “Oh, I've read it twice already! Take it back, please.”

1.text: Return the book to the library
1.done: The book goes back to its shelf.

job.flour.title: Flour for the Bakery
job.flour.text: {giver} from the bakery: “We're out of flour, and the bread slicer still has work to do!”

0.text: Bring flour to the bakery
0.done: The baker starts kneading straight away.

job.ball_on_roof.title: A Ball on the Roof
job.ball_on_roof.text: {giver} threw a ball onto the shed roof. You can't reach it without a ladder.

0.text: Ask the firefighters to get the ball down
0.done: The firefighter laughs: “Easiest job all week”

1.text: Give the ball back to the little one
1.done: The ball flies again — this time well away from the roof.

job.photo.title: A Photo for the Paper
job.photo.text: {giver} from the newsroom: the issue needs a photo — {place}. The photographer is at the other end of the village.

0.text: Take a photo: {place}
0.done: Click! The light is just right.

1.text: Take the photo to the newspaper office
1.done: The photo goes into the issue.

job.umbrella.title: An Umbrella in the Rain
job.umbrella.text: A downpour! {giver} is stuck at the bus stop without an umbrella.

0.text: Borrow an umbrella from the shop
0.done: The shopkeeper lends you her own — old, but in one piece.

1.text: Take the umbrella to the square
1.done: It's a squeeze for two under one umbrella, but you stay dry.

job.snow_path.title: Clear the Path
job.snow_path.text: Snowed in! {giver} can't get out of the gate.

0.text: Clear the path to the gate
0.done: A shovel, snow, rosy cheeks. There's a path!

job.milk.title: Milk for the Cheese Dairy
job.milk.text: {giver} from “Ovechka”: the cheese moulds are waiting, but there isn't enough milk.

0.text: Milk a cow at the farm

1.text: Bring the milk to “Ovechka”
1.done: The milk is still warm — the cheese will turn out well.

job.stray.title: The Cat by the Vet's
job.stray.text: {giver} from the vet's: there's a hungry cat under the porch again.

0.text: Catch a fish

1.text: Feed the cat

job.water.title: Water for {giver}
job.water.text: It's scorching. {giver} hasn't the strength to carry water from the well.

0.text: Draw water from the well at the farm

1.text: Bring the water
1.done: So cold it makes your teeth ache.

job.letter.title: A Letter for the Post
job.letter.text: {giver} has written a letter to the grandchildren, but can't make it to the post office.

0.text: Send the letter at the post office
0.done: A postmark, a stamp — and off the letter flies.

job.groceries.title: Bread for {giver}
job.groceries.text: {giver} asks you to buy some bread — their legs won't cooperate today.

0.text: Buy a palianytsia at the bakery

1.text: Deliver the bread
1.done: “Still warm! Sit down, I'll pour you some tea”

work.cafe.name: A Shift at the “Lypa” Café
work.cafe.start: The apron hangs on the hook by the door. Guests are already taking their tables — to the counter!
work.cafe.thanks: Thank you — it was easy with you today. Come again, the guests like you.

work.bakery.name: A Shift at the Bakery
work.bakery.start: The dough rose before dawn. Hands in the flour — and to the oven!
work.bakery.thanks: The whole street smells of it. Thanks for the help — without you I'd never have made it by opening time.

work.post.name: Sorting at the Post Office
work.post.start: A mountain of parcels today. Sort them onto the shelves by address, and Lina will deliver them.
work.post.thanks: Everything's on its shelf. Lina has already set off on her rounds — thanks for the help!

work.farm.name: A Day at the Farm
work.farm.start: Boots by the cowshed door. On the farm the day starts early!
work.farm.thanks: There we go, the animals are seen to. You're a fine pair of hands — come again.

work.library.name: An Hour at the Library
work.library.ask: {who} returns a book — to the “{what}” shelf
work.library.start: There's a whole trolley of returned books. Please put them back on the shelves.
work.library.thanks: Look how neat they are! Thank you — now everyone will find what they're looking for.

work.flowers.name: A Shift at “Pivonia”
work.flowers.start: The flowers are in their buckets, the ribbons on their spools. Whoever comes in first gets the best bouquet.
work.flowers.thanks: Everyone left with their own bouquet. Thank you — you've a light touch with flowers.

work.grocery.name: A Shift at the “Kolosok” Till
work.grocery.start: The till is open, the change in the drawer. The first customer already has a basket!
work.grocery.thanks: The till balanced to the kopiyka. Thank you — the queue melts away with you.

work.clothes.name: A Shift at “Lion”
work.clothes.start: The hangers are straight, the mirror wiped. Someone’s already trying on a jacket!
work.clothes.thanks: Everyone left in something that suits them. Thank you — you have an eye for it.

work.salon.name: A Shift at “Lokon”
work.salon.start: The scissors are sharp, the towels warm. Come in, take a seat!
work.salon.thanks: Everyone left looking lovely. Thank you — the day flies by with you.

work.hardware.name: A Shift at “Maister”
work.hardware.start: The shelves are full, the keys on the hook. Who’s first for nails?
work.hardware.thanks: Everything was found, even in the farthest corner. Thanks for the help!

work.donuts.name: A Shift at the Donut Shop
work.donuts.start: The donuts are still hot, the sugar in the sieve. The smell is already calling people in!
work.donuts.thanks: The tray’s empty to the last crumb. Thank you — donuts taste better with you.

work.creamery.name: A Shift at “Ovechka”
work.creamery.start: Cheese on the shelves, yarn in the baskets. We’re open!
work.creamery.thanks: Everything sold, even the socks. Thank you — come again.

work.vet.name: A Shift at “Lapka”

options.1: a dog with a sore paw

work.vet.start: The coat is on the hook, the log on the desk. Someone in the queue is barking already!
work.vet.thanks: Every tail has been seen to. Thank you — the animals love you.

work.bar.name: An Evening Behind the Bar at “Zhabka”
work.bar.start: The glasses shine, the music is soft. The first guests are at the bar!
work.bar.thanks: A good evening it was. Thank you — the bar is merry with you behind it.

work.hostel.name: A Shift at the “Leleka” Front Desk
work.hostel.start: The keys are on the board, the guest book open. Someone’s here with a suitcase already!
work.hostel.thanks: The guests are settled and happy. Thank you for your kind heart.

work.sto.name: A Shift at the “Haika” Garage
work.sto.start: The spanners are laid out, gloves on. The first car is pulling in!
work.sto.thanks: Everyone drove off in working cars. Thank you — you have golden hands.

work.newsroom.name: A Shift at the “Lypove Herald”
work.newsroom.ask: A new piece for the “{what}” section
work.newsroom.start: The news has piled up. Sort it into sections — we print tomorrow!
work.newsroom.thanks: The paper is laid out. Thank you — tomorrow the whole town will read it.

work.radio.name: A Shift at “Lypove FM”
work.radio.start: The microphone is warm, the records on the shelf. We’re on air!
work.radio.thanks: The listeners call to say thanks. And so do I — it was a lovely show.

home.lypova.name: Your house on Linden Street
home.lypova.text: The house where it all began.

flat.sadova.1.name: Ground-floor flat
flat.sadova.1.text: Two rooms, windows onto the street; in the morning you can hear the street waking up.

flat.sadova.2.name: Flat with a balcony
flat.sadova.2.text: Second floor, a balcony full of flowers, and a view across the roofs all the way to the church.

house.prodayetsya.name: Two-storey house for sale
house.prodayetsya.text: Roomy, with an attic and a little garden. The owners moved to their daughter's in the city.

cottage.lis.name: Cottage at the edge of the forest
cottage.lis.text: Quiet, pine trees, and hares hopping under the window in the morning.

plot.pole.1.name: Garden plot No. 1
plot.pole.1.text: A few beds by the road: carrots, potatoes, and greens in summer.

plot.pole.2.name: Garden plot No. 2
plot.pole.2.text: A few beds by the road: carrots, potatoes, and greens in summer.

proj.bandstand.name: A bandstand in the park
proj.bandstand.text: The park needs music: we're raising money for a bandstand by the lake, for an orchestra to play in and for dancing on holidays.
proj.bandstand.done: The bandstand in the park is open! On weekend evenings a brass band will play there — everyone's welcome.

proj.library_roof.name: A new roof for the library
proj.library_roof.text: The library roof leaks: buckets stand under the drips and the books are hidden under plastic. Let's re-roof it together.
proj.library_roof.done: The library has a new roof — not one more drop on the books! The librarian thanks everyone who helped.

proj.farm_lights.name: Lights on the road to the farm
proj.farm_lights.text: In winter the farmers come home in the dark: let's put up streetlights along the road to the farm.
proj.farm_lights.done: The road to the farm is lit now. The farmers say even the cows walk to the barn more calmly in the evening.

proj.playground.name: A playground on Nova Street
proj.playground.text: There are little ones growing up on Nova Street and nowhere to play. Swings, a slide, a sandpit — and a bench for the parents.
proj.playground.done: A playground has opened on Nova Street — you can hear the children laughing all the way to the square.

proj.riverside.name: A garden by the stream
proj.riverside.text: The bank of the stream is overgrown with weeds. Let's make a little garden there: benches, flowerbeds, lamps — a place for evening walks.
proj.riverside.done: There's a new garden by the stream: benches, flowerbeds and lamps. They say the first proposal has already happened there.

open.icecream.name: Ice-cream kiosk
open.icecream.text: An ice-cream kiosk has opened by the park: vanilla, cherry and pistachio. Summer has officially begun!

open.coffee_cart.name: Coffee cart
open.coffee_cart.text: A coffee cart has appeared on the square — hot coffee and tea to go for cold mornings.

open.flower_cart.name: The flower cart
open.flower_cart.text: Spring! The flower cart is back on the square: tulips, daffodils and the first snowdrops.

open.book_stall.name: Book stall
open.book_stall.text: A book stall has opened by the library: old and new books for a few coins.

open.tech.name: The “Tekhnika” counter
open.tech.text: The post office has opened a “Tekhnika” counter: smartphones with a camera, a map and the weather forecast.

open.tech_laptops.name: Laptops at the post office
open.tech_laptops.text: Laptops have appeared at the “Tekhnika” counter. The café is already asking whether people can sit with them until lunch.

bed.broken: A slat has cracked — you won't get a good night's sleep in this bed

fridge.broken: The fridge doesn't cool — food won't keep in it

stove.broken: The stove won't light — the gas hisses, but there's no flame

vesnianka.name: Come Out, Come Out, Little Sun

lines.0: Have a seat. Before the wheel — your eyes. The signs tell you everything you need to know, if you read them.
lines.1: A red circle — a ban or a limit. A blue square — a hint: a crossing, parking, a hospital.
lines.2: A triangle with a red border — caution. “Children” by the school means your foot is already over the brake.
lines.3: A solid line — don't cross it. A broken line — you may, if you can see far ahead.

lines.0: In town it's fifty. Not because it says so, but because a child could run out from behind any car.
lines.1: By the school it's twenty. Children don't look at the road, they look at each other.
lines.2: A wet road — you brake for longer. Snow — longer still. There's no need to hurry in Lypove: everything's closed for lunch anyway.

2.title: Zebra Crossings and Right of Way

lines.0: A white zebra crossing is the pedestrian's ground. If someone is standing on it or walking up to it — you stop too.
lines.1: Don't honk at a granny crossing the road. She was walking this way back when they still carted hay here.
lines.2: At a junction without lights, give way to whoever's on your right. The main road is the main road — but not for the reckless.

lines.0: The pavement is for feet, not wheels. Even “just for a minute” — it's a fine and a disgrace.
lines.1: Park at the side of the road or on the gravel by the garage. Not in front of a gate, not on a zebra crossing.
lines.2: Got out? Look behind you. The cyclist wants to get home too.
lines.3: That's it. Now the theory. I'll ask the way life will ask.

0.q: How fast can you drive in town?

answers.2: As fast as the road allows

1.q: There's a “Children” sign by the school. What do you do?

answers.0: Honk so they get out of the way
answers.2: Drive past faster while nobody's around

lastivka.name: Lastivka
lastivka.text: A small green runabout, twenty years on the road. The doors shut on the second try, but it starts in the frost.

dnipro.name: Dnipro
dnipro.text: A cream saloon with one previous owner — a teacher. It smells of books and mint sweets.

poltava.name: Poltava
poltava.text: A blue estate with a roof rack: it fits a Christmas tree, a sack of potatoes and the whole family.

khvylia.name: Khvylia
khvylia.text: A small sky-blue city car: it parks anywhere, and filling the tank costs about a coffee.

kalyna.name: Kalyna
kalyna.text: A red saloon with soft seats and an old radio that only picks up Lypove FM.

buran.name: Buran
buran.text: Nearly new, from the doctor's garage: quiet, warm in winter and reliable in any weather.

cellmate.0: Your cellmate rolls over: “You in for speeding too? I'm in for a chicken. It was crossing, I braked… long story.”
cellmate.1: “You sleep best here at five in the morning. Just when they let you out.”
cellmate.2: “The officer on duty is called Stepan. Ask politely for tea and he'll give you some — with sugar, even.”
cellmate.3: In the dark someone has scratched on the wall: “Petro was here. Won't do it again.” Below, in another hand: “Me neither.”
cellmate.4: “You know what's worst? Not the bunk. It's that tomorrow the paper will write about you.”
cellmate.5: Your cellmate sighs: “My wife says I drive like the house is on fire. But I just like my music loud.”
cellmate.6: Beyond the bars a clock ticks in the corridor. You can hear it like a heartbeat — slow and steady.

donut_site.name: Ponchykova
donut_site.done: “Ponchykova” has opened on the edge of town! Glazed donuts, sprinkled donuts, donuts with cherry jam — and coffee to go with them. The first customers were queuing before it even opened.

home_old1.name: Old house on Garden Street
home_old1.why: the owners went to their daughter's in Poland and have locked up the house for now.
home_old1.back: a young family from Zhytomyr has moved in — they're already planting flowers under the windows.

home_old2.name: Grandpa Ostap's cottage on Garden Street
home_old2.why: Grandpa Ostap moved to his son's in the regional capital. The neighbours look after the garden.
home_old2.back: a teacher and her husband bought the house — they say it'll have the prettiest porch on the street.

build.kitchen.name: Kitchen
build.kitchen.text: A stove, a fridge, a work wall with cupboards and a round table by the window.

build.bedroom.name: Bedroom
build.bedroom.text: A bed with bedside tables and lamps, a wardrobe, a rug.

build.bath.name: Bathroom
build.bath.text: A bath, a washbasin with a mirror, a towel on the warm pipe.

build.workshop.name: Workshop
build.workshop.text: A workbench under the window, a chest for materials, shelves for tools.

build.music.name: Music room
build.music.text: Oak panelling for a good sound, room for a piano and an armchair to listen in.

build.attic.name: Attic
build.attic.text: Right under the roof: a swing, an old chest, a folding mattress and fairy lights.

build.cellar.name: Cellar
build.cellar.text: A cool stone cellar for provisions and old things.

build.upstairs.name: Upstairs
build.upstairs.text: Stairs going up, a bright study and another bedroom — for guests or a nursery.

build.terrace.name: Terrace
build.terrace.text: Wooden decking under the sky: a lounger, a table for dinner outdoors, a grill.

build.yard.name: Yard
build.yard.text: A yard of your own with an apple tree, a swing and a sandpit.

turtle.name: Tortoise
turtle.text: An old, calm tortoise looking for a home. Loves water, warmth and taking things slowly.

fox.name: Fox
fox.text: A red fox from a den in the forest. Slow to trust — you'll have to leave food out for her a few times.

robot.name: Robot helper
robot.text: A small household robot. Charges from the socket, beeps when happy, and now and then needs a screwdriver.

dragon.name: Little dragon
dragon.text: From a warm egg found beyond the rift. Sleeps on coins and warms the room.
